sentences.zh: 【漢紀三十二】起旃蒙作噩，盡柔兆閹茂，凡二年。

translations.literal: 【Han Records 32】 From Zhanmeng Zuoe through Rouzhao Yanmao—in all, two years.
translations.idiomatic: 【Han Records 32】 From the first year of the Zhanmeng cycle through the last year of the Rouzhao cycle—two years in all.

sentences.zh: 世祖光武皇帝上之上

translations.literal: Founding Emperor Guangwu, Upper Part 1, First Section.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor Guangwu — Upper Part 1, First Section.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，方望與安陵人弓林共立前定安公嬰為天子，聚黨數千人，居臨涇。

translations.literal: 1. In spring, the first month, Fang Wang together with Gong Lin of Anling jointly set up the former Duke of Ding'an, Ying, as Son of Heaven; they gathered a faction of several thousand men and dwelt at Linjing.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In spring, in the first month, Fang Wang and Gong Lin of Anling jointly enthroned the former Duke of Ding'an, Liu Ying, as emperor; they gathered several thousand followers and encamped at Linjing.

sentences.zh: 更始遣丞相松等擊破，皆斬之。

translations.literal: Gengshi sent Chancellor Song and others to defeat and break them; all were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The Gengshi Emperor sent Chancellor Song and others to rout them; all were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 2鄧禹至箕關，擊破河東都尉，進圍安邑。

translations.literal: 2. Deng Yu reached Jiguan Pass, defeated and broke the Hedong commandant, and advanced to besiege Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: 2. Deng Yu reached Jiguan Pass, routed the Hedong commandant, and advanced to besiege Anyi.

sentences.zh: 3赤眉二部俱會弘農。

translations.literal: 3. The two divisions of the Red Eyebrows both assembled at Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: 3. The two divisions of the Red Eyebrows united at Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 更始遣討難將軍蘇茂拒之；

translations.literal: Gengshi sent the Pacify-Difficulty General Su Mao to resist them;
translations.idiomatic: The Gengshi Emperor sent Pacify-Difficulty General Su Mao to resist them;

sentences.zh: 茂軍大敗。

translations.literal: Mao's army was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Su Mao's army was routed.

sentences.zh: 赤眉眾遂大集，乃分萬人為一營，凡三十營。

translations.literal: The Red Eyebrow host thereupon gathered in great numbers; they then divided ten thousand men to a camp—in all thirty camps.
translations.idiomatic: The Red Eyebrows then massed in force, organizing ten thousand men per camp—thirty camps in all.

sentences.zh: 三月，更始遣丞相松與赤眉戰於蓩鄉，松等大敗，死者三萬餘人。

translations.literal: In the third month, Gengshi sent Chancellor Song to fight the Red Eyebrows at Maoxiang; Song and the others were utterly defeated, and more than thirty thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Gengshi Emperor sent Chancellor Song against the Red Eyebrows at Maoxiang; Song was routed and more than thirty thousand men were killed.

sentences.zh: 赤眉遂轉北至湖。

translations.literal: The Red Eyebrows thereupon turned and marched north to Hu.
translations.idiomatic: The Red Eyebrows then turned north toward Hu.

sentences.zh: 4蜀郡功曹李熊說公孫述宜稱天子。

translations.literal: 4. Li Xiong, merit-clerk of Shu Commandery, urged Gongsun Shu that he ought to style himself Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: 4. Li Xiong, merit-clerk of Shu Commandery, urged Gongsun Shu to declare himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，述即帝位，號成家，改元龍興；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Shu took the emperor's position, styled his state Chengjia, and changed the era name to Longxing;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Gongsun Shu took the throne, named his state Chengjia, and adopted the era name Longxing;

translations.literal: Ren Gui of Yuexi held the commandery and surrendered to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Gui of Yuexi held the commandery and submitted to Gongsun Shu.

sentences.zh: 5蕭王北擊尤來、大槍、五幡於元氏，追至北平，連破之；

translations.literal: 5. The Prince of Xiao marched north to attack Youlai, Daqiang, and Wufan at Yuanshi, pursued them to Beiping, and defeated them repeatedly;
translations.idiomatic: 5. The Prince of Xiao marched north against Youlai, Daqiang, and Wufan at Yuanshi, pursued them to Beiping, and defeated them in succession;

sentences.zh: 又戰於順水北，乘勝輕進，反為所敗。

translations.literal: they fought again north of the Shun River; riding victory he pressed lightly forward and was in turn defeated by them.
translations.idiomatic: he fought again north of the Shun River; pressing his advantage too boldly, he was routed in turn.

sentences.zh: 王兄子在南陽，何憂無主！

translations.literal: The prince's elder brother's son is in Nanyang—why worry that there is no lord!"
translations.idiomatic: The prince's nephew sits in Nanyang—why fear we lack a leader?"

translations.literal: " The host was fearful; only after several days did they settle.
translations.idiomatic: " The army was terrified; several days passed before order returned.

sentences.zh: 賊雖戰勝，而憚王威名，夜，遂引去。

translations.literal: Though the bandits had won the battle, they feared the prince's awesomeness and name; at night they thereupon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Though the rebels had won, they feared the prince's renown; that night they withdrew.

translations.idiomatic: </ref> They fought repeatedly and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 賊退入漁陽，所過虜掠。

translations.literal: The bandits retreated into Yuyang and plundered wherever they passed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fell back into Yuyang, plundering as they went.

sentences.zh: 強弩將軍陳俊言於王曰：「賊無輜重，宜令輕騎出賊前，使百姓各自堅壁以絕其食，可不戰而殄也。

translations.literal: The Powerful Crossbow General Chen Jun said to the prince: "The bandits have no baggage train; it is fitting to send light cavalry out ahead of them and make the hundred surnames each strengthen their walls to cut off their food—they can be exterminated without fighting."
translations.idiomatic: Powerful Crossbow General Chen Jun told the prince, "The rebels carry no baggage. Send light cavalry ahead of them and order the people to fortify their walls and cut off their supplies—you can destroy them without a battle."

sentences.zh: 」王然之，遣俊將輕騎馳出賊前，視人保壁堅完者，敕令固守；

translations.literal: " The prince approved, sent Jun to lead light cavalry galloping out ahead of the bandits, and wherever he saw people whose fortified walls were firm and complete, he ordered them to hold fast;
translations.idiomatic: " The prince agreed and sent Chen Jun with light cavalry racing ahead of the enemy; wherever he found villages with strong defenses, he ordered them to hold firm;

sentences.zh: 放散在野者，因掠取之。

translations.literal: those scattered in the open fields he released to be seized and taken.
translations.idiomatic: whatever grain lay in the open fields he seized for the army.

sentences.zh: 賊至，無所得，遂散敗。

translations.literal: When the bandits arrived they obtained nothing and thereupon scattered in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels arrived they found nothing and broke apart in defeat.

sentences.zh: 王謂俊曰：「困此虜者，將軍策也。

translations.literal: The prince said to Jun: "To have trapped these captives—this was the general's stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: The prince told Chen Jun, "To have trapped these foes was your stratagem."

sentences.zh: 6馮異遺李軼書，為陳禍福，勸令歸附蕭王；

translations.literal: 6. Feng Yi sent a letter to Li Yi, setting forth fortune and misfortune and urging him to submit to the Prince of Xiao;
translations.idiomatic: 6. Feng Yi wrote to Li Yi, laying out fortune and ruin and urging him to submit to the Prince of Xiao;

sentences.zh: 軼知長安已危，而以伯升之死，心不自安，乃報書曰：「軼本與蕭王首謀造漢，今軼守洛陽，將軍鎮孟津，俱據機軸，千載一會，思成斷金。

translations.literal: Yi knew Chang'an was already in peril, yet because of Bo Sheng's death his heart was not at ease; he thereupon replied: "Yi originally with the Prince of Xiao first plotted to create Han; now Yi holds Luoyang while the general garrisons Mengjin—we both hold the pivot of the realm, a meeting once in a thousand years; I think to forge metal that will not break."
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi knew Chang'an was doomed, yet Liu Xiu's brother's death left him uneasy. He replied, "I first plotted with the Prince of Xiao to restore Han. Now I hold Luoyang while you garrison Mengjin—we both grip the empire's pivot. Such a meeting comes once in a thousand years; let us forge a bond that will not break."

sentences.zh: 唯深達蕭王，願進愚策以佐國安民。

translations.literal: Only deeply convey this to the Prince of Xiao; I wish to advance foolish counsel to aid the state and settle the people."
translations.idiomatic: Convey my words faithfully to the prince; I wish to offer humble counsel to aid the realm and comfort the people."

sentences.zh: 」軼自通書之後，不復與異爭鋒，故異得北攻天井關，拔上黨兩城，又南下河南成皋以東十三縣，降者十餘萬。

translations.literal: " From the time Yi opened correspondence he no longer contended with Yi in arms; therefore Yi was able to attack north at Tianjing Pass, take two cities of Shangdang, and again march south through thirteen counties east of Chenggao in Henan—those who submitted numbered more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: " After this exchange Li Yi ceased fighting Feng Yi, who marched north against Tianjing Pass, took two cities in Shangdang, then swept south through thirteen counties east of Chenggao in Henan—more than a hundred thousand submitted.

sentences.zh: 武勃將萬餘人攻諸畔者，異與戰於士鄉下，大破，斬勃；

translations.literal: Wu Bo led more than ten thousand men to attack those who had rebelled; Yi fought him below Shixiang, routed him utterly, and beheaded Bo;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Bo led more than ten thousand men against the defectors; Feng Yi met him at Shixiang, routed his force, and beheaded Wu Bo;

sentences.zh: 軼閉門不救。

translations.literal: Yi shut his gates and did not rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi shut his gates and would not rescue him.

sentences.zh: 異見其信效，具以白王。

translations.literal: Yi saw his trustworthiness and effectiveness and reported it all to the prince.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yi, seeing this proof of good faith, reported everything to the prince.

sentences.zh: 王報異曰：「季文多詐，人不能得其要領。

translations.literal: The prince replied to Yi: "Jiwen is full of deceit—men cannot grasp his essential point."
translations.idiomatic: The prince replied, "Jiwen is treacherous; no one can read his true intent."

sentences.zh: 今移其書告守、尉當警備者。

translations.literal: Now circulate his letter and inform every defender and commandant who ought to be on guard."
translations.idiomatic: Now circulate his letter and warn every garrison commander to stand alert."

sentences.zh: 」眾皆怪王宣露軼書；

translations.literal: " All wondered at the prince's revealing Yi's letter;
translations.idiomatic: " All marveled that the prince had exposed Li Yi's letter;

sentences.zh: 朱鮪聞之，使人刺殺軼，由是城中乖離，多有降者。

translations.literal: Zhu Wei heard of it and sent men to assassinate Yi; from this the city fell into division and many submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wei heard of it and had Li Yi assassinated; the city split apart and many defected.

sentences.zh: 朱鮪聞王北征而河內孤，乃遣其將蘇茂、賈彊將兵三萬餘人渡鞏河，攻溫；

translations.literal: Zhu Wei, hearing the prince had marched north while Henei stood isolated, thereupon sent his generals Su Mao and Jia Qiang leading more than thirty thousand troops across the Gong River to attack Wen;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wei, learning the prince had marched north leaving Henei exposed, sent Su Mao and Jia Qiang with more than thirty thousand men across the Gong River to attack Wen;

sentences.zh: 鮪自將數萬人攻平陰以綴異。

translations.literal: Wei himself led several tens of thousands to attack Pingyin in order to pin Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wei himself led tens of thousands against Pingyin to tie down Feng Yi.

sentences.zh: 檄書至河內，寇恂即勒軍馳出，並移告屬縣，發兵會溫下。

translations.literal: When the dispatch reached Henei, Kou Xun immediately mustered his army and galloped out, and at the same time sent notice to subordinate counties to raise troops and assemble below Wen.
translations.idiomatic: When the dispatch reached Henei, Kou Xun mustered his troops at once, notified the subordinate counties, and raced to Wen with every man he could raise.

sentences.zh: 軍吏皆諫曰：「今洛陽兵渡河，前後不絕。

translations.literal: The army officers all remonstrated, saying: "Now Luoyang's troops are crossing the river, front and rear without break."
translations.idiomatic: His officers all urged caution: "Luoyang's troops are crossing the river in an unbroken stream."

sentences.zh: 宜待眾軍畢集，乃可出也。

translations.literal: "It is fitting to wait until all armies are fully gathered—only then may we go out."
translations.idiomatic: "We should wait until every force has assembled before we march out."

sentences.zh: 」恂曰：「溫，郡之籓蔽，失溫則郡不可守。

translations.literal: " Xun said: "Wen is the commandery's outer shield; lose Wen and the commandery cannot be held."
translations.idiomatic: " Kou Xun said, "Wen is this commandery's shield; lose Wen and Henei cannot be held."

sentences.zh: 」遂馳赴之。

translations.literal: " He thereupon galloped to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: " He raced to its relief.

sentences.zh: 旦日，合戰，而馮異遣救及諸縣兵適至，恂令士卒乘城鼓噪大呼，言曰：「劉公兵到！

translations.literal: At dawn they joined battle; Feng Yi had sent relief and the county troops just arrived; Xun ordered his soldiers to mount the walls, beat drums, shout loudly, and cry: "Lord Liu's troops have arrived!"
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the armies clashed; Feng Yi's relief force and the county levies arrived just then. Kou Xun ordered his men onto the walls to drum and shout, "Lord Liu's army is here!"

sentences.zh: 」蘇茂軍聞之，陳動。

translations.literal: " Su Mao's army heard it and their formation wavered.
translations.idiomatic: " Su Mao's ranks wavered at the cry.

sentences.zh: 恂因奔擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Xun thereupon charged and struck; he routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Xun charged and routed them.

sentences.zh: 馮異亦渡河擊朱鮪，鮪走；

translations.literal: Feng Yi also crossed the river to attack Zhu Wei; Wei fled;
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yi crossed the river as well and struck Zhu Wei, who fled;

sentences.zh: 異與恂追至洛陽，環城一匝而歸。

translations.literal: Yi together with Xun pursued to Luoyang, circled the city once, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yi and Kou Xun pursued to Luoyang, circled the walls once, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 自是洛陽震恐，城門晝閉。

translations.literal: From this Luoyang trembled in terror; the city gates were shut by day.
translations.idiomatic: From that day Luoyang trembled; the gates stayed shut even in daylight.

sentences.zh: 異、恂移檄上狀，諸將入賀，因上尊號。

translations.literal: Yi and Xun sent dispatches reporting upward; the generals entered to congratulate him and thereupon offered the exalted title.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yi and Kou Xun sent memorials reporting their victory; the generals came to congratulate the prince and pressed the exalted title upon him.

sentences.zh: 將軍南陽馬武先進曰：「大王雖執謙退，奈宗廟社稷何！

translations.literal: The general Ma Wu of Nanyang advanced first and said: "Great King, though you hold to modest withdrawal, what of the ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain!"
translations.idiomatic: General Ma Wu of Nanyang spoke first: "Your Highness clings to modesty, but what of the ancestral temples and the altars of state?"

sentences.zh: 宜先即尊位，乃議征伐。

translations.literal: "It is fitting first to take the exalted position, and only then deliberate on campaigns."
translations.idiomatic: "Take the throne first, then plan your campaigns."

sentences.zh: 今此誰賊而馳騖擊之乎？

translations.literal: "Who are these bandits now that you gallop and rush to strike them?"
translations.idiomatic: "Who are these foes that you still ride out to strike?"

sentences.zh: 」王驚曰：「何將軍出此言！

translations.literal: " The prince startled and said: "General He, how can you speak such words!"
translations.idiomatic: " The prince started and said, "General He, how dare you speak so!"

sentences.zh: 可斬也！

translations.literal: "You may be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: "You deserve execution!"

sentences.zh: 」乃引軍還薊。

translations.literal: " He thereupon led his army back to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: " He led his army back to Ji.

sentences.zh: 復遣吳漢率耿弇、景丹等十三將軍追尤來等，斬首萬三千餘級，遂窮追至浚靡而還。

translations.literal: He again sent Wu Han leading Geng Yan, Jing Dan, and twelve other generals—thirteen in all—to pursue Youlai and the others; they beheaded more than thirteen thousand and pressed the pursuit to the limit at Junmi before returning.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wu Han with Geng Yan, Jing Dan, and twelve other generals—thirteen in all—to pursue Youlai and his band; they took more than thirteen thousand heads and chased them to Junmi before turning back.

sentences.zh: 賊散入遼西、遼東，為烏桓、貊人所鈔擊略盡。

translations.literal: The bandits scattered into Liaoxi and Liaodong and were raided and struck by the Wuhuan and Mo peoples until nearly all were gone.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels scattered into Liaoxi and Liaodong; the Wuhuan and Mo peoples raided them until scarcely any remained.

sentences.zh: 都護將軍賈復與五校戰於真定，復傷瘡甚。

translations.literal: The Protector-General Jia Fu fought the Five Commandants at Zhending; Fu's wounds were severe.
translations.idiomatic: Protector-General Jia Fu fought the Five Commandants at Zhending and was gravely wounded.

sentences.zh: 王大驚曰：「我所以不令賈復別將者，為其輕敵也。

translations.literal: The prince was greatly startled and said: "The reason I did not let Jia Fu command a separate force was that he treats the enemy lightly."
translations.idiomatic: The prince was deeply alarmed and said, "I refused to let Jia Fu command a separate force because he is reckless before the enemy."

sentences.zh: 果然，失吾名將！

translations.literal: "As expected—I have lost my famed general!"
translations.idiomatic: "As I feared—I have lost a great general!"

sentences.zh: 聞其婦有孕，生女邪，我子娶之；

translations.literal: "I hear his wife is with child: if a girl is born, my son shall marry her;
translations.idiomatic: "I hear his wife is with child. If she bears a daughter, my son shall marry her;

sentences.zh: 生男邪，我女嫁之；

translations.literal: if a boy is born, my daughter shall marry him;
translations.idiomatic: if a son, my daughter shall marry him;

sentences.zh: 不令其憂妻子也。

translations.literal: I will not let him grieve over wife and children."
translations.idiomatic: he shall not grieve for wife or child."

sentences.zh: 」復病尋愈，追及王於薊，相見甚歡。

translations.literal: " Fu's illness soon healed; he pursued and overtook the prince at Ji, and their meeting was very joyful.
translations.idiomatic: " Jia Fu soon recovered, overtook the prince at Ji, and their reunion was joyful.

sentences.zh: 還至中山，諸將復上尊號；

translations.literal: Returning to Zhongshan, the generals again offered the exalted title;
translations.idiomatic: On the return to Zhongshan the generals again pressed the exalted title upon him;

sentences.zh: 王又不聽。

translations.literal: the prince again would not heed them.
translations.idiomatic: again he refused.

sentences.zh: 行到南平棘，諸將復固請之；

translations.literal: Marching to Nanpingji, the generals again firmly pressed him;
translations.idiomatic: At Nanpingji the generals pressed him again;

sentences.zh: 王不許。

translations.literal: the prince did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: again he refused.

sentences.zh: 諸將且出，耿純進曰：「天下士大夫，捐親戚，棄土壤，從大王於矢石之間者，其計固望攀龍鱗，附鳳翼，以成其所志耳。

translations.literal: As the generals were about to withdraw, Geng Chun advanced and said: "The gentlemen of the realm who have cast aside kin, abandoned their native soil, and followed the Great King amid flying stones and arrows—their plan has always been to climb the dragon's scales and cling to the phoenix's wings, to fulfill the aims they cherish."
translations.idiomatic: As the generals were leaving, Geng Chun stepped forward and said, "The scholars who abandoned kin and homeland to follow Your Highness through arrow and stone did so hoping to touch the dragon's scales and cling to the phoenix's wings—to fulfill their ambitions."

sentences.zh: 今大王留時逆眾，不正號位，純恐士大夫望絕計窮，則有去歸之思，無為久自苦也。

translations.literal: "Now the Great King lingers, going against the host, and will not set right his title and rank; Chun fears the gentlemen's hopes will end and their plans reach exhaustion—then they will think of leaving and returning. Do not long afflict yourself for nothing."
translations.idiomatic: "Now you linger against the will of your followers and will not take the throne. I fear that when their hopes fail and their plans reach an end, they will think of leaving you. Do not torment yourself—and us—any longer."

sentences.zh: 大眾一散，難可復合。

translations.literal: Once the great host scatters, it is hard to reunite.
translations.idiomatic: Once the great host scatters, it is hard to reunite.

sentences.zh: 」純言甚誠切，王深感曰：「吾將思之。

translations.literal: " Chun's words were very sincere and earnest; the King was deeply moved and said: "I shall think on it.
translations.idiomatic: " Chun's words were very sincere and earnest; the King was deeply moved and said: "I shall think on it.

sentences.zh: 行至鄗，召馮異〔詣鄗〕<ref>召馮異〔詣鄗〕章校「十二行本『異』下有『詣鄗』二字；

translations.literal: When he reached Hao he summoned Feng Yi [to come to Hao]<ref>Summon Feng Yi [to Hao]: Zhang's collation notes that the twelve-line edition has the two characters "to Hao" after "Yi";
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Hao he summoned Feng Yi [to come to Hao]<ref>Summon Feng Yi [to Hao]: Zhang's collation notes that the twelve-line edition has the two characters "to Hao" after "Yi";

sentences.zh: 乙十一行本同；

translations.literal: the Yi eleven-line edition agrees;
translations.idiomatic: the Yi eleven-line edition agrees;

sentences.zh: 孔本同；

translations.literal: Kong's edition agrees;
translations.idiomatic: Kong's edition agrees;

sentences.zh: 張校同。

translations.literal: Zhang's collation agrees.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang's collation agrees.

translations.literal: " The Book of the Later Han, biography of Feng Yi, agrees; supplied on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: " The Book of the Later Han, biography of Feng Yi, agrees; supplied on that authority.

sentences.zh: </ref>，問四方動靜。

translations.literal: </ref> and asked about conditions in the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: </ref> and asked about conditions in the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 異曰：「更始必敗，宗廟之憂在於大王，宜從眾議！

translations.literal: Yi said: "Gengshi is certain to fail; the ancestral temple's peril lies with the Great King—you ought to follow the multitude's counsel!
translations.idiomatic: Yi said: "The Gengshi Emperor is certain to fail; the peril to the ancestral temple lies with you, Great King—you ought to follow the multitude's counsel!

sentences.zh: 」會儒生強華自關中奉《赤伏符》來詣王曰：「劉秀髮兵捕不道，四夷雲集龍鬬野，四七之際火為主。

translations.literal: " It happened that the scholar Qiang Hua from within the passes presented the Red Talisman and came to the King, saying: "Liu Xiu raises troops to seize the lawless; the four barbarians gather like clouds, dragons contend in the wilds; at the juncture of four and seven, Fire is master.
translations.idiomatic: " It happened that the scholar Qiang Hua from within the passes presented the Red Talisman and came to the King, saying: "Liu Xiu raises troops to seize the lawless; the four barbarians gather like clouds, dragons contend in the wilds; at the juncture of four and seven, Fire is master.

sentences.zh: 」群臣因復奏請。

translations.literal: " The ministers thereupon again memorialized and requested.
translations.idiomatic: " The ministers thereupon again memorialized and requested.

sentences.zh: 六月，己未，王即皇帝位于鄗南；

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day jiwei, the King ascended the imperial throne south of Hao;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the day jiwei, the King ascended the imperial throne south of Hao;

sentences.zh: 改元，大赦。

translations.literal: he changed the era name and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: he changed the era name and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 7鄧禹圍安邑，數月未下，更始大將軍樊參將數萬人度大陽，欲攻禹。

translations.literal: 7 Deng Yu besieged Anyi for several months without taking it; Gengshi's Grand General Fan Can led several tens of thousands across Dayang, intending to attack Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yu besieged Anyi for several months without taking it; the Gengshi Emperor's Grand General Fan Can led several tens of thousands across Dayang, intending to attack Yu.

sentences.zh: 禹逆擊於解南，斬之。

translations.literal: Yu met and struck him south of Jie and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu met and struck him south of Jie and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 王匡、成丹、劉均合軍十餘萬，復共擊禹，禹軍不利。

translations.literal: Wang Kuang, Cheng Dan, and Liu Jun combined armies of more than a hundred thousand and again jointly attacked Yu; Yu's army was unfavorable.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kuang, Cheng Dan, and Liu Jun combined armies of more than a hundred thousand and again attacked Yu together; Yu's army fared badly.

sentences.zh: 明日，癸亥，匡等以六甲窮日，不出，禹因得更治兵。

translations.literal: The next day, on the day guihai, Kuang and the others, because it was the last day of the six jia cycle, did not come out; Yu thereby was able to reorganize his troops again.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, on the day guihai, Kuang and the others, because it was the last day of the six jia cycle, did not come out; Yu thereby was able to reorganize his troops.

sentences.zh: 甲子，匡悉軍出攻禹。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, Kuang led out his entire army to attack Yu.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiazi, Kuang led out his entire army to attack Yu.

sentences.zh: 禹令軍中無得妄動，既至營下，因傳發諸將，鼓而並進，大破之。

translations.literal: Yu ordered that within the army none might move rashly; when they had reached below the camp, he then transmitted orders to the generals, drummed, and advanced together, routing them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Yu ordered that none in the army move rashly; when they had reached below the camp, he transmitted orders to the generals, drummed, and advanced together, routing them utterly.

sentences.zh: 匡等皆走，禹追斬均及河東太守楊寶，遂定河東，匡等奔還長安。

translations.literal: Kuang and the others all fled; Yu pursued and beheaded Jun and Hedong Administrator Yang Bao, thereupon pacified Hedong, and Kuang and the others fled back to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang and the others all fled; Yu pursued and beheaded Liu Jun and Hedong Administrator Yang Bao, thereby pacified Hedong, and Kuang and the others fled back to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 張卬與諸將議曰：「赤眉旦暮且至，見滅不久，不如掠長安，東歸南陽；

translations.literal: Zhang Ang and the generals deliberated, saying: "The Red Eyebrows will arrive before long; our destruction is not far off—better to plunder Chang'an and return east to Nanyang;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ang and the generals deliberated, saying: "The Red Eyebrows will arrive before long; our destruction is not far off—better to plunder Chang'an and return east to Nanyang;

sentences.zh: 事若不集，復入湖池中為盜耳！

translations.literal: if the affair does not succeed, we can again enter the lake marshes and be bandits!
translations.idiomatic: if the affair does not succeed, we can again take to the lake marshes and be bandits!

sentences.zh: 」乃共入，說更始；

translations.literal: " They then together entered and urged Gengshi;
translations.idiomatic: " They then together entered and urged the Gengshi Emperor;

sentences.zh: 更始怒不應，莫敢復言。

translations.literal: Gengshi was angry and did not assent; none dared speak again.
translations.idiomatic: The Gengshi Emperor was angry and did not assent; none dared speak again.

sentences.zh: 更始使王匡、陳牧、成丹、趙萌屯新豐，李松軍槁，以拒赤眉。

translations.literal: Gengshi sent Wang Kuang, Chen Mu, Cheng Dan, and Zhao Meng to garrison Xinfeng, and Li Song's army at Gao, to resist the Red Eyebrows.
translations.idiomatic: The Gengshi Emperor sent Wang Kuang, Chen Mu, Cheng Dan, and Zhao Meng to garrison Xinfeng and Li Song's army at Gao to resist the Red Eyebrows.

sentences.zh: 張卬、廖湛、胡殷、申屠建與隗囂合謀，欲以立秋日貙膢時共劫更始，俱成前計。

translations.literal: Zhang Ang, Liao Zhan, Hu Yin, Shentu Jian, and Wei Ao together plotted, wishing on the day of Beginning of Autumn at the time of the autumn sacrifice jointly to seize Gengshi and together carry out the earlier plan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ang, Liao Zhan, Hu Yin, Shentu Jian, and Wei Ao plotted together to seize the Gengshi Emperor on the day of Beginning of Autumn at the time of the autumn sacrifice and carry out their earlier plan.

sentences.zh: 更始知之，託病不出，召張卬等入，將悉誅之，唯隗囂稱疾不入，會客王遵、周宗等勒兵自守。

translations.literal: Gengshi learned of it, pleaded illness and did not come out, summoned Zhang Ang and the others in, and was about to execute them all; only Wei Ao claimed illness and did not enter, while his guests Wang Zun, Zhou Zong, and others mustered troops to defend themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The Gengshi Emperor learned of it, pleaded illness and did not appear, summoned Zhang Ang and the others in, and was about to execute them all; only Wei Ao claimed illness and did not enter, while his guests Wang Zun, Zhou Zong, and others mustered troops to defend themselves.

sentences.zh: 更始狐疑不決，卬、湛、殷疑有變，遂突出。

translations.literal: Gengshi was hesitant and could not decide; Ang, Zhan, and Yin suspected there was a change and thereupon broke out.
translations.idiomatic: The Gengshi Emperor hesitated and could not decide; Ang, Zhan, and Yin suspected a trap and broke out.

sentences.zh: 獨申屠建在，更始斬建，使執金吾鄧曄將兵圍隗囂第。

translations.literal: Only Shentu Jian remained; Gengshi beheaded Jian and sent Bearer of the Mace Deng Ye to lead troops and besiege Wei's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Only Shentu Jian remained; the Gengshi Emperor beheaded him and sent Bearer of the Mace Deng Ye to lead troops and besiege Wei's residence.

sentences.zh: 卬、湛、殷勒兵燒門，入戰宮中，更始大敗。

translations.literal: Ang, Zhan, and Yin mustered troops, burned the gates, entered and fought within the palace, and Gengshi was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Ang, Zhan, and Yin mustered troops, burned the gates, fought within the palace, and the Gengshi Emperor was utterly defeated.

sentences.zh: 囂亦潰圍，走歸天水。

translations.literal: Ao also broke the siege and fled back to Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Ao also broke the siege and fled back to Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 明旦，更始東奔趙萌於新豐。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day, Gengshi fled east to Zhao Meng at Xinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the next day, the Gengshi Emperor fled east to Zhao Meng at Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 更始復疑王匡、陳牧、成丹與張卬等同謀，乃並召入；

translations.literal: Gengshi again suspected Wang Kuang, Chen Mu, and Cheng Dan of plotting with Zhang Ang and the others, and therefore summoned them all in;
translations.idiomatic: The Gengshi Emperor again suspected Wang Kuang, Chen Mu, and Cheng Dan of plotting with Zhang Ang and the others and summoned them all in;

sentences.zh: 牧、丹先至，即斬之。

translations.literal: Mu and Dan arrived first and were immediately beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Mu and Dan arrived first and were immediately beheaded.

sentences.zh: 王匡懼，將兵入長安，與張卬等合。

translations.literal: Wang Kuang was afraid, led troops into Chang'an, and joined Zhang Ang and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kuang was afraid, led troops into Chang'an, and joined Zhang Ang and the others.

sentences.zh: 8赤眉進至華陰，軍中有齊巫，常鼓舞祠城陽景王，巫狂言：「景王大怒曰：『當為縣官，何故為賊！

translations.literal: 8 The Red Eyebrows advanced to Huayin; in the army there was a Qi shaman who often drummed and danced in sacrifice to King Jing of Chengyang; the shaman raved, saying: "King Jing was greatly angered and said: 'You ought to serve as officials of the state—why act as bandits!
translations.idiomatic: The Red Eyebrows advanced to Huayin; in the army there was a Qi shaman who often drummed and danced in sacrifice to King Jing of Chengyang; the shaman raved, saying: "King Jing was greatly angered and said: 'You ought to serve as officials of the state—why act as bandits!

sentences.zh: 』」有笑巫者輒病，軍中驚動。

translations.literal: '" Whoever laughed at the shaman immediately fell ill, and the army was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: '" Whoever laughed at the shaman immediately fell ill, and the army was shaken.

sentences.zh: 方望弟陽說樊崇等曰：「今將軍擁百萬之眾，西向帝城，而無稱號，名為群賊，不可以久。

translations.literal: Fang Wang's younger brother Yang urged Fan Chong and the others, saying: "Now the general holds a host of a million men and faces west toward the imperial city, yet has no title—you are called a band of thieves; this cannot last long.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Wang's younger brother Yang urged Fan Chong and the others, saying: "Now you hold a host of a million men and face west toward the imperial city, yet have no title—you are called a band of thieves; this cannot last.

sentences.zh: 不如立宗室，挾義誅伐，以此號令，誰敢不從！

translations.literal: Better to establish a member of the imperial clan, take righteousness as your banner for punitive campaigns, and with such a command—who would dare not follow!
translations.idiomatic: Better to establish a member of the imperial clan, take righteousness as your banner for punitive campaigns, and with such a command—who would dare not follow!

sentences.zh: 」崇等以為然，而巫言益甚。

translations.literal: " Chong and the others thought it right, but the shaman's words grew ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: " Chong and the others agreed, but the shaman's words grew ever stronger.

sentences.zh: 前至鄭，乃相與議曰：「今迫近長安，而鬼神若此，當求劉氏共尊立之。

translations.literal: When they advanced to Zheng, they then deliberated together, saying: "Now we press close to Chang'an, and the spirits and ghosts are thus—we ought to seek out the Liu clan and together honor and establish one.
translations.idiomatic: When they advanced to Zheng, they deliberated together, saying: "Now we press close to Chang'an, and the spirits are thus—we ought to seek out the Liu clan and together honor and establish one.

sentences.zh: 先是，赤眉過式，掠故式侯萌之子恭、茂、盆子三人自隨。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Red Eyebrows passed through Shi, they seized and took along the former Marquis of Shi's sons Gong, Mao, and Penzi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Red Eyebrows passed through Shi, they seized and took along the former Marquis of Shi's sons Gong, Mao, and Penzi.

sentences.zh: 恭少習《尚書》，隨樊崇等降更始於洛陽，復封式侯，為侍中，在長安。

translations.literal: Gong in youth studied the Documents; he followed Fan Chong and the others in surrendering to Gengshi at Luoyang, was again enfeoffed as Marquis of Shi, made Palace Attendant, and was in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Gong had studied the Documents in youth; he followed Fan Chong and the others in surrendering to the Gengshi Emperor at Luoyang, was again enfeoffed as Marquis of Shi, made Palace Attendant, and was in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 茂與盆子留軍中，屬右校卒史劉俠卿，主牧牛。

translations.literal: Mao and Penzi remained in the army, attached to Right Column company clerk Liu Xiaqing, who was in charge of herding cattle.
translations.idiomatic: Mao and Penzi remained in the army under Right Column company clerk Liu Xiaqing, who was in charge of herding cattle.

sentences.zh: 及崇等欲立帝，求軍中景王後，得七十餘人，唯茂、盆子及前西安侯孝最為近屬。

translations.literal: When Chong and the others wished to establish an emperor, they sought descendants of King Jing in the army and found more than seventy; only Mao, Penzi, and the former Marquis of Xi'an Xiao were closest in kinship.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong and the others wished to establish an emperor, they sought descendants of King Jing in the army and found more than seventy; only Mao, Penzi, and the former Marquis of Xi'an Xiao were closest in kinship.

sentences.zh: 崇等曰：「聞古者天子將兵稱上將軍。

translations.literal: Chong and the others said: "We have heard that in antiquity when the Son of Heaven led troops he was styled supreme general.
translations.idiomatic: Chong and the others said: "We have heard that in antiquity when the Son of Heaven led troops he was styled supreme general.

sentences.zh: 」乃書札為符曰：「上將軍」。

translations.literal: " They then wrote on slips as talismans the words "supreme general."
translations.idiomatic: " They then wrote on slips as talismans the words "supreme general."

sentences.zh: 又以兩空札置笥中，於鄭北設壇場，祠城陽景王，諸三老、從事皆大會。

translations.literal: They also placed two blank slips in a box; north of Zheng they set up an altar platform, sacrificed to King Jing of Chengyang, and all the village elders and staff officers held a great assembly.
translations.idiomatic: They also placed two blank slips in a box; north of Zheng they set up an altar, sacrificed to King Jing of Chengyang, and all the village elders and staff officers held a great assembly.

sentences.zh: 列盆子等三人居中立，以年次探札，盆子最幼，後探，得符；

translations.literal: They arrayed Penzi and the three others standing in the center; by order of age they drew slips—Penzi was youngest and drew last, and obtained the talisman;
translations.idiomatic: They arrayed Penzi and the three others standing in the center; by order of age they drew slips—Penzi was youngest and drew last, and obtained the talisman;

sentences.zh: 諸將皆稱臣，拜。

translations.literal: all the generals styled themselves subjects and bowed.
translations.idiomatic: all the generals styled themselves subjects and bowed.

sentences.zh: 盆子時年十五，被發徙跣，敝衣赭汗，見眾拜，恐畏欲啼。

translations.literal: Penzi was then fifteen years old, hair unbound, barefoot, in tattered clothes stained with red sweat; when he saw the multitude he bowed, afraid and on the verge of weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Penzi was then fifteen, hair unbound and barefoot, in tattered clothes stained with red sweat; when he saw the multitude he bowed, afraid and on the verge of weeping.

sentences.zh: 茂謂曰：「善臧符！

translations.literal: Mao said to him: "Guard the talisman well!
translations.idiomatic: Mao said to him: "Guard the talisman well!

sentences.zh: 」盆子即齧折，棄之。

translations.literal: " Penzi immediately bit it in two and threw it away.
translations.idiomatic: " Penzi immediately bit it in two and threw it away.

sentences.zh: 以徐宣為丞相，樊崇為御史大夫，逢安為左大司馬，謝祿為右大司馬，其餘皆列卿、將軍。

translations.literal: They made Xu Xuan Chancellor, Fan Chong Censor-in-Chief, Feng An Left Grand Marshal, Xie Lu Right Grand Marshal, and the rest were all ranked as ministers and generals.
translations.idiomatic: They made Xu Xuan Chancellor, Fan Chong Censor-in-Chief, Feng An Left Grand Marshal, Xie Lu Right Grand Marshal, and the rest were all ranked as ministers and generals.

sentences.zh: 盆子雖立，猶朝夕拜劉俠卿，時欲出從牧兒戲；

translations.literal: Though Penzi was established, he still morning and evening bowed to Liu Xiaqing and at times wished to go out and follow the herdboys in play;
translations.idiomatic: Though Penzi was established, he still morning and evening bowed to Liu Xiaqing and at times wished to go out and play with the herdboys;

sentences.zh: 俠卿怒止之，崇等亦不復候視也。

translations.literal: Xiaqing angrily stopped him, and Chong and the others also no longer attended and looked in on him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaqing angrily stopped him, and Chong and the others also no longer attended him.

sentences.zh: 9秋，七月，辛未，帝使使持節拜鄧禹為大司徒，封酇侯，食邑萬戶；

translations.literal: 9 In autumn, the seventh month, on the day xinwei, the Emperor sent an envoy bearing the staff of authority to appoint Deng Yu Grand Master of Works, enfeoff him as Marquis of Zan, with a fief of ten thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day xinwei, the Emperor sent an envoy bearing the staff of authority to appoint Deng Yu Grand Master of Works, enfeoff him as Marquis of Zan, with a fief of ten thousand households;

sentences.zh: 禹時年二十四。

translations.literal: Yu was then twenty-four years old.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was then twenty-four years old.

sentences.zh: 又議選大司空，帝以《赤伏符》曰「王梁主衛作玄武」，丁丑，以野王令王梁為大司空。

translations.idiomatic: At the time troops were rising throughout the empire; Zhan alone remained tranquil and comforted the common people.

sentences.zh: 門下督謀為湛起兵，湛收斬之。

translations.idiomatic: A gate-house supervisor plotted to raise troops for Zhan; Zhan seized and beheaded him.

translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned Zhan as Master of Writing and had him oversee and fix the old regulations.

sentences.zh: 又以鄧禹西征，拜湛為司直，行大司徒事。

sentences.zh: 車駕每出征伐，常留鎮守。

translations.literal: Whenever the imperial carriage went out on punitive campaigns, Zhan was regularly left to garrison and guard.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the imperial carriage went on campaign, Zhan was regularly left to garrison and guard.

translations.literal: Yu again defeated them and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Yu again defeated them and drove them off.

translations.literal: A clansman, Liu Mao, gathered a host between Jing and Mi, styled himself Resist-the-New General, attacked and took Yingchuan and Runan, and his host numbered more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The clansman Liu Mao gathered a host between Jing and Mi, styled himself Resist-the-New General, took Yingchuan and Runan, and mustered more than a hundred thousand.

translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Rapid Cavalry Grand General Jing Dan, Establish Authority Grand General Geng Yan, and Strong Crossbow General Chen Jun to attack him.

translations.idiomatic: Li Song led his troops back from Gao, followed the Gengshi Emperor, and together with Zhao Meng attacked Wang Kuang and Zhang Ang in Chang'an.

translations.literal: They fought continuously for more than a month; Kuang and the others were defeated and fled, and Gengshi moved his residence to Changxin Palace.
translations.idiomatic: They fought continuously for more than a month; Kuang and the others were defeated and fled, and the Gengshi Emperor moved to Changxin Palace.

sentences.zh: 赤眉至高陵，王匡、張卬等迎降之，遂共連兵進攻東都門。

translations.literal: The Red Eyebrows reached Gaoling; Wang Kuang, Zhang Ang, and the others came out to welcome and surrender to them, and thereupon together linked forces and advanced to attack the Eastern Capital Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Red Eyebrows reached Gaoling; Wang Kuang, Zhang Ang, and the others came out to welcome and surrender to them, and together advanced to attack the Eastern Capital Gate.

translations.idiomatic: Li Song went out to fight; the Red Eyebrows captured him alive.

translations.idiomatic: Song's younger brother Kuang was Colonel of the City Gates and opened the gate to admit them.

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Red Eyebrows entered Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Red Eyebrows entered Chang'an.

translations.literal: Gengshi fled alone on horseback and went out through the Kitchen City Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Gengshi Emperor fled alone on horseback and went out through the Kitchen City Gate.

translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Shi Gong, because the Red Eyebrows had established his younger brother, bound himself and entered the imperial prison;

translations.literal: hearing that Gengshi had been defeated and fled, then came out and met King of Dingtao Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: hearing that the Gengshi Emperor had been defeated and fled, then came out and met King of Dingtao Liu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 祉為之除械，相與從更始於渭濱。

translations.literal: Zhi removed his bonds for him, and together they followed Gengshi on the Wei bank.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi removed his bonds and together they followed the Gengshi Emperor on the Wei bank.

translations.literal: Right Assistant Commandant Yan Ben, fearing he would lose Gengshi and be executed by the Red Eyebrows, immediately took Gengshi to Gaoling; Ben led troops to lodge and guard him—in fact he surrounded him.
translations.idiomatic: Right Assistant Commandant Yan Ben, fearing he would lose the Gengshi Emperor and be executed by the Red Eyebrows, immediately took him to Gaoling; Ben led troops to lodge and guard him—in fact he surrounded him.

sentences.zh: 更始將相皆降赤眉，獨丞相曹竟不降，手劍格死。

translations.literal: Gengshi's generals and ministers all surrendered to the Red Eyebrows; only Chancellor Cao Jing did not surrender and was killed fighting hand to hand with his sword.
translations.idiomatic: The Gengshi Emperor's generals and ministers all surrendered to the Red Eyebrows; only Chancellor Cao Jing did not surrender and was killed fighting hand to hand with his sword.

sentences.zh: 13辛未，詔封更始為淮陽王；

translations.literal: 13 On the day xinwei an edict enfeoffed Gengshi as King of Huaiyang;
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinwei an edict enfeoffed the Gengshi Emperor as King of Huaiyang;

translations.literal: officials or common people who dared harm him were guilty of the same crime as great treason;
translations.idiomatic: any official or commoner who dared harm him was guilty of the same crime as great treason;

sentences.zh: 其送詣吏者封列侯。

translations.literal: whoever delivered him to the authorities was enfeoffed as a ranked marquis.
translations.idiomatic: whoever delivered him to the authorities was enfeoffed as a ranked marquis.

translations.literal: 14 Earlier, Zhuo Mao of Wan was broad, benevolent, respectful, and loving, tranquil and easy and delighting in the Way, refined and solid and not making a showy appearance; in conducting himself he stood between the clear and the turbid—from tying his hair until white-haired old age he never had contention or rivalry with others; fellow villagers and old friends, though conduct and ability differed from Mao's, all loved and admired him with joy.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhuo Mao of Wan was broad, benevolent, respectful, and loving, tranquil and easy and delighting in the Way, refined and solid without showy appearance; in conduct he stood between the clear and the turbid—from youth until white-haired old age he never quarreled with anyone; fellow villagers and old friends, though their conduct and ability differed from his, all loved and admired him gladly.

sentences.zh: 哀、平間為密令，視民如子，舉善而教，口無惡言，吏民親愛，不忍欺之。

translations.idiomatic: Between the Ai and Ping reigns he was magistrate of Mi, regarded the people as children, promoted the good and taught them, and never spoke evil words; officials and people were affectionate toward him and could not bear to deceive him.

translations.idiomatic: " The people said, "I have heard that a worthy and enlightened ruler makes the people unafraid of officials and officials do not take from the people."

translations.idiomatic: " Mao said, "You are a benighted commoner!"

translations.literal: The reason ordinary men can dwell together without disorder and differ from birds and beasts is that they have benevolence, love, ritual, and righteousness and know how to respect and serve one another.
translations.idiomatic: The reason people can live together without disorder and differ from birds and beasts is that they have benevolence, ritual, and righteousness and know how to respect and serve one another.

sentences.zh: 汝獨不欲修之，寧能高飛遠走，不在人間邪！

translations.literal: You alone do not wish to cultivate them—can you fly high and run far and not be among men?!
translations.idiomatic: You alone refuse to cultivate them—can you fly away and live apart from mankind?!"

sentences.zh: 吏顧不當乘威力強請求耳。

translations.literal: The official surely ought not to use his power to force demands.
translations.idiomatic: The official surely ought not to use his power to force demands.

sentences.zh: 亭長素善吏，歲時遺之，禮也。

translations.literal: The station chief has long been on good terms with the official; giving him gifts at the seasons is ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: The station chief has long been on good terms with the official; giving him seasonal gifts is proper courtesy.

sentences.zh: 」民曰：「苟如此，律何故禁之？

translations.idiomatic: " The people said, "If so, why does the law forbid it?"

sentences.zh: 」茂笑曰：「律設大法，禮順人情。

translations.literal: " Mao laughed and said: "The law sets forth the great standard; ritual accords with human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: " Mao laughed and said, "The law sets forth the great standard; ritual accords with human feeling.

translations.literal: Now if I teach you by ritual, you will surely harbor no resentment;
translations.idiomatic: Now if I teach you by ritual, you will surely harbor no resentment;

translations.idiomatic: if I govern you by the law, where will you set hand or foot?!"

translations.idiomatic: Mao took no offense and governed affairs as before.

translations.idiomatic: When Wang Mang held the regency, he was dismissed on grounds of illness and returned home.

translations.literal: When the Emperor took the throne, he first sought out Mao; Mao was then more than seventy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor took the throne, he first sought out Mao; Mao was then more than seventy.

translations.idiomatic: On jiashen an edict said, "One whose fame crowns all under Heaven ought to receive the realm's weightiest reward.

translations.idiomatic: Now Mao is made Grand Tutor and enfeoffed as Marquis of Praising Virtue."

translations.literal: Your servant Guang says: Confucius praised "raise the good and teach; where one cannot, then exhort," and therefore Shun raised Gao Yao, Tang raised Yi Yin, and the unbenevolent kept their distance—because there was virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang comments: Confucius praised "raise the good and teach; where one cannot, then exhort," and therefore Shun raised Gao Yao and Tang raised Yi Yin, and the unbenevolent kept their distance—because virtue was present.

sentences.zh: 光武即位之初，群雄競逐，四海鼎沸，彼摧堅陷敵之人，權略詭辯之士，方見重於世，而獨能取忠厚之臣，旌循良之吏，拔於草萊之中，實諸群公之首，宜其光復舊物，享祚久長，蓋由知所先務而得其本原故也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangwu's accession, rival heroes contended in pursuit and the four seas seethed like a cauldron; those who shattered the hard and overran the foe, and masters of power-stratagem and crafty debate, were just then valued in the world—yet he alone could take loyal and honest ministers, honor diligent and good officials, draw them from among the weeds, and place them at the head of all the lords. sentences.zh: 辛卯，朱鮪面縛，與岑彭俱詣河陽。

translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Zhu Wei came with his face bound and, together with Cen Peng, went to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 帝解其縛，召見之，復令彭夜送鮪歸城。

translations.idiomatic: The Emperor undid his bonds, summoned and received him, and again ordered Peng to escort Wei back to the city by night.

sentences.zh: 明旦，與蘇茂等悉其眾出降。

translations.idiomatic: At dawn the next day he and Su Mao and the others led out all their forces to surrender.

sentences.zh: 拜鮪為平狄將軍，封扶溝侯；

translations.literal: Wei was appointed Pacify-the-Di General and enfeoffed as Marquis of Fugou;
translations.idiomatic: Wei was appointed Pacify-the-Di General and enfeoffed as Marquis of Fugou;

translations.idiomatic: later he became Minister Steward, and the fief was transmitted through generations.

sentences.zh: 帝使侍御史河內杜詩安集洛陽。

translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Attendant Censor Du Shi of Henei to settle and pacify Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 將軍蕭廣縱兵士暴橫，詩敕曉不改，遂格殺廣。

translations.literal: General Xiao Guang let his soldiers run violent and overbearing; Shi admonished and instructed him but he did not reform, and Shi thereupon killed Guang on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: General Xiao Guang let his soldiers run violent and overbearing; Shi admonished him but he did not reform, and Shi thereupon killed Guang on the spot.

sentences.zh: 還，以狀聞。

translations.literal: On returning, he reported the matter in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: On returning, he reported the matter in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 上召見，賜以棨戟，遂擢任之。

translations.literal: The sovereign summoned him, bestowed upon him a ceremonial halberd, and thereupon promoted and employed him.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign summoned him, bestowed a ceremonial halberd upon him, and thereupon promoted and employed him.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，癸丑，車駕入洛陽，幸南宮，遂定都焉。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on guichou, the imperial carriage entered Luoyang, visited the Southern Palace, and thereupon fixed the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on guichou, the imperial carriage entered Luoyang, visited the Southern Palace, and thereupon made it the capital.

sentences.zh: 16赤眉下書曰：「聖公降者，封為長沙王；

translations.literal: 16. The Chimei issued a document, saying: "If the Sacred Lord surrenders, he shall be enfeoffed as King of Changsha;
translations.idiomatic: 16. The Chimei issued a document, saying, "If the Sacred Lord surrenders, he shall be enfeoffed as King of Changsha;

translations.idiomatic: " The Gengshi Emperor sent Liu Gong to request surrender; the Chimei sent their general Xie Lu to receive him.

sentences.zh: 更始隨祿，肉袒，上璽綬於盆子。

translations.idiomatic: The Gengshi Emperor followed Lu, bared his torso, and presented the seal and cord to Penzi.

translations.idiomatic: The Chimei seated the Gengshi Emperor in the courtyard and were about to kill him;

sentences.zh: 劉恭、謝祿為請，不能得，遂引更始出。

translations.literal: Liu Gong and Xie Lu pleaded for him but could not prevail, and thereupon led the Gengshi Emperor out.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gong and Xie Lu pleaded for him but could not prevail, and thereupon led the Gengshi Emperor out.

sentences.zh: 劉恭追呼曰：「臣誠力極，請得先死！

translations.literal: Liu Gong ran after them calling: "Your servant has truly exhausted his strength—may I be allowed to die first!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gong ran after them calling, "Your servant has truly exhausted his strength—may I be allowed to die first!"

sentences.zh: 」拔劍欲自刎。

translations.literal: " He drew his sword intending to kill himself.
translations.idiomatic: " He drew his sword intending to kill himself.

sentences.zh: 樊崇等遽共救止之。

translations.literal: Fan Chong and the others hastily together rescued and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Chong and the others hastily rescued and stopped him.

sentences.zh: 乃赦更始，封為畏威侯。

translations.literal: They then pardoned the Gengshi Emperor and enfeoffed him as Marquis Who Fears Authority.
translations.idiomatic: They then pardoned the Gengshi Emperor and enfeoffed him as Marquis Who Fears Authority.

sentences.zh: 劉恭復為固請，竟得封長沙王。

translations.literal: Liu Gong again firmly pleaded, and in the end he was enfeoffed as King of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gong pleaded again firmly, and in the end he was enfeoffed as King of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 更始常依謝祿居，劉恭亦擁護之。

translations.literal: The Gengshi Emperor regularly lodged with Xie Lu, and Liu Gong also protected and supported him.
translations.idiomatic: The Gengshi Emperor regularly lodged with Xie Lu, and Liu Gong also protected and supported him.

sentences.zh: 17劉盆子居長樂宮，三輔郡縣、營長遣使貢獻，兵士輒剽奪之，又數暴掠吏民，由是皆復固守。

translations.literal: 17. Liu Penzi dwelt in Changle Palace; commanderies and counties of the Three Metropolises and camp chiefs sent envoys with tribute, but the soldiers repeatedly plundered it, and again and again violently looted officials and commoners—whereupon all again held firm in defense.
translations.idiomatic: 17. sentences.zh: 百姓不知所歸，聞鄧禹乘勝獨克而師行有紀，皆望風相攜負以迎軍，降者日以千數，眾號百萬。

translations.literal: The common people did not know where to turn; hearing that Deng Yu, riding victory and advancing alone, had discipline in his army's march, they all at the mere report of wind carried one another on their backs to welcome the army—those surrendering numbered thousands daily, and the host was styled a million.
translations.idiomatic: The common people did not know where to turn; hearing that Deng Yu, riding victory and advancing alone, kept discipline in his army's march, they all at the mere report of his approach carried one another on their backs to welcome the army—surrenders numbered thousands daily, and the host was styled a million.

sentences.zh: 禹所止，輒停車拄節以勞來之，父老、童稚，垂發、戴白滿其車下，莫不感悅，於是名震關西。

translations.literal: Wherever Yu halted, he would stop his carriage, lean on his staff, and comfort and welcome them; elders and children, hair hanging down and heads white, filled the area beneath his carriage—none failed to be moved and pleased; thereby his fame shook Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Yu halted, he would stop his carriage, lean on his staff, and comfort and welcome them; elders and children, with hanging hair and white heads, filled the area beneath his carriage—none failed to be moved and pleased; thereby his fame shook Guanxi.

sentences.zh: 諸將豪傑皆勸禹徑攻長安，禹曰：「不然。

translations.literal: The various generals and heroes all urged Yu to strike straight at Chang'an; Yu said: "It is not so.
translations.idiomatic: The various generals and heroes all urged Yu to strike straight at Chang'an; Yu said, "It is not so.

sentences.zh: 今吾眾雖多，能戰者少，前無可仰之積，後無轉饋之資；

translations.literal: Now though our host is many, those who can fight are few; ahead there is no accumulated store to rely on, behind no resources for turning and supplying;
translations.idiomatic: Now though our host is many, those who can fight are few; ahead there is no accumulated store to rely on, behind no resources for turning and supplying;

sentences.zh: 赤眉新拔長安，財穀充實，鋒銳未可當也。

translations.literal: the Chimei have newly taken Chang'an; wealth and grain are full, and their sharp edge cannot yet be faced.
translations.idiomatic: the Chimei have newly taken Chang'an; wealth and grain are full, and their sharp edge cannot yet be faced.

sentences.zh: 夫盜賊群居無終日之計，財穀雖多，變故萬端，寧能堅守者也！

translations.literal: Bandits dwelling in a mass have no plan for a full day; though wealth and grain are many, changes and turns are myriad—how could they hold firm for long!
translations.idiomatic: Bandits dwelling in a mass have no plan for a full day; though wealth and grain are many, changes are myriad—how could they hold firm for long!"

sentences.zh: 上郡、北地、安定三郡，土廣人稀，饒穀多畜，吾且休兵北道，就糧養士，以觀其敝，乃可圖也。

translations.literal: Shang, Beidi, and Anding—the three commanderies—have broad land and sparse people, abundant grain and many livestock; I shall for now rest the troops on the northern road, draw near grain to nourish the soldiers, watch for their exhaustion, and then it may be plotted.
translations.idiomatic: Shang, Beidi, and Anding—the three commanderies—have broad land and sparse people, abundant grain and many livestock; I shall for now rest the troops on the northern road, draw on grain to nourish the soldiers, watch for their exhaustion, and then we may act."

sentences.zh: 」於是引軍北至栒邑，所到，諸營保郡邑皆開門歸附。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he led the army north to Xunyi; wherever he arrived, the various fortified camps, commanderies, and counties all opened their gates and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he led the army north to Xunyi; wherever he arrived, fortified camps, commanderies, and counties all opened their gates and submitted.

sentences.zh: 18上遣岑彭擊荊州群賊，下犨、葉等十餘城。

translations.literal: 18. The Emperor sent Cen Peng to attack the bandit hosts of Jingzhou and took more than ten cities including Zuan and Ye.
translations.idiomatic: 18. The Emperor sent Cen Peng to attack the bandit hosts of Jingzhou and took more than ten cities including Zuan and Ye.

sentences.zh: 19十一月，甲午，上幸懷。

translations.literal: 19. In the eleventh month, on jiawu, the Emperor visited Huai.
translations.idiomatic: 19. In the eleventh month, on jiawu, the Emperor visited Huai.

translations.literal: 20. Liu Yong of Liang again declared himself emperor at Suiyang.
translations.idiomatic: 20. Liu Yong of Liang again declared himself emperor at Suiyang.

translations.idiomatic: 22. The Three Metropolises suffered under Chimei violence and tyranny; all pitied the Gengshi Emperor and wished to steal him out;

translations.literal: Zhang Yin and others were deeply troubled by this and had Xie Lu strangle him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yin and others were deeply troubled by this and had Xie Lu strangle him to death.

translations.literal: Liu Gong went by night, gathered and stored his corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gong went by night and gathered and stored his corpse.

translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Deng Yu to bury him at Baling.

translations.literal: Gentleman of the Palace Zhao Xi of Wan was about to go out through Wuguan; on the road he met the Gengshi Emperor's kin—all barefoot, hungry, and in distress; Xi exhausted his funds and grain to give them and escorted them forward.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman of the Palace Zhao Xi of Wan was about to go out through Wuguan; on the road he met the Gengshi Emperor's kin—all barefoot, hungry, and in distress; Xi exhausted his funds and grain to give them and escorted them forward.

translations.literal: The King of Wan, Liu Ci, heard of it and welcomed them back to their native district.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wan, Liu Ci, heard of it and welcomed them back to their native district.

translations.idiomatic: 23. Wei Ao returned to Tianshui, again gathered his forces, revived his former enterprise, and styled himself Supreme General of the Western Provinces.

translations.idiomatic: Kuang said, "You have great talent and ought to mature late.

translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon went to Beidi for farming and herding.

translations.idiomatic: He often told his guests, "A man in setting his aim—when poor ought to grow firmer, when old ought to grow stronger."

translations.literal: " He then distributed it all among kin and old friends.
translations.idiomatic: " He then distributed it all among kin and old friends.

translations.literal: Hearing that Wei Ao loved scholars, he went to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Wei Ao loved scholars, he went to join him.

sentences.zh: 囂其敬重，與決籌策。

translations.literal: Ao greatly respected him and settled plans and stratagems with him.
translations.idiomatic: Ao greatly respected him and settled plans and stratagems with him.

translations.literal: Ban Biao was the son of Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Biao was the son of Zhi.

translations.literal: Hexi is rich and prosperous, girded by the river and secure; Zhangye Dependent State has ten thousand crack horsemen—if urgency comes, block the river crossings and it is enough for self-defense—this is a place to preserve one's line!

translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon through Meng requested to go to Hexi.

translations.literal: Meng recommended Rong to the Gengshi Emperor, and he was made Commandant of Zhangye Dependent State.
translations.idiomatic: Meng recommended Rong to the Gengshi Emperor, and he was made Commandant of Zhangye Dependent State.

translations.literal: Once Rong had arrived, he soothed and bound bold champions, embraced and gathered Qiang and barbarians—he won their hearts exceedingly.
translations.idiomatic: Once Rong had arrived, he soothed and bound bold champions, won over the Qiang and other tribes, and gained their hearts completely.

sentences.zh: 及更始敗，融與梁統等計議曰：「今天下擾亂，未知所歸。

translations.literal: When Gengshi fell, Rong with Liang Tong and others deliberated: "Now the realm is disturbed—no one knows where to turn.
translations.idiomatic: When Gengshi fell, Rong deliberated with Liang Tong and others, saying, "The realm is in turmoil and no one knows where to turn.

sentences.zh: 河西斗絕在羌、胡中，不同心戮力，則不能自守，權鈞力齊，復無以相率，當推一人為大將軍，共全五部，觀時變動。

translations.literal: Hexi stands alone amid Qiang and Hu—without one heart and joined strength we cannot hold ourselves; powers equal and forces matched, again none can lead the rest—we should push one man as grand general, jointly preserve the five commanderies, and watch how the times change.
