sentences.zh: 以位次，咸共推梁統；

translations.literal: By rank in office, all together pushed Liang Tong;
translations.idiomatic: By rank in office, all together pushed Liang Tong;

sentences.zh: 統固辭，乃推融行河西五郡大將軍事。

translations.literal: Tong firmly declined, and they then pushed Rong to act as grand general over Hexi's five commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Tong firmly declined, and they then pushed Rong to act as grand general over Hexi's five commanderies.

sentences.zh: 武威太守馬期、張掖太守任仲並孤立無黨，乃共移書告示之，二人即解印綬去。

translations.literal: Wuwei Administrator Ma Qi and Zhangye Administrator Ren Zhong were both isolated without factions; they jointly sent a letter to announce this—the two at once surrendered seal and cord and left.
translations.idiomatic: Wuwei Administrator Ma Qi and Zhangye Administrator Ren Zhong were both isolated without factions; they jointly sent a proclamation to them, and the two at once surrendered their seals and cords and departed.

sentences.zh: 於是以梁統為武威太守，史苞為張掖太守，竺曾為酒泉太守，辛肜為敦煌太守。

translations.literal: Thereupon Liang Tong was made Wuwei Administrator, Shi Bao Zhangye Administrator, Zhu Ceng Jiuquan Administrator, Xin Yin Dunhuang Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Liang Tong was made Wuwei Administrator, Shi Bao Zhangye Administrator, Zhu Ceng Jiuquan Administrator, and Xin Yin Dunhuang Administrator.

sentences.zh: 融居屬國，領都尉職如故；

translations.literal: Rong remained in the dependent state, holding commandant duties as before;
translations.idiomatic: Rong remained in the dependent state and held his commandant's duties as before;

sentences.zh: 置從事，監察五郡。

translations.literal: he appointed attendants to oversee the five commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: he appointed attendants to oversee the five commanderies.

sentences.zh: 河西民俗質樸，而融等政亦寬和，上下相親，晏然富殖。

translations.literal: Hexi's customs were plain and simple, and Rong and the others' government was also lenient and mild—superiors and inferiors were close, and in peace they grew rich.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi's people were plain by custom, and Rong and the others governed leniently and mildly; superiors and inferiors drew close, and in peace the region grew prosperous.

sentences.zh: 修兵馬，習戰射，明烽燧，羌、胡犯塞，融輒自將與諸郡相救，皆如符要，每輒破之。

translations.literal: They trained horses and arms, practiced battle and archery, made beacon fires clear—when Qiang and Hu raided the passes Rong always led in person with the commanderies to rescue; all matched the tally and tally-string, and each time he broke them.
translations.idiomatic: They trained horses and arms, practiced battle and archery, and kept the beacon fires clear; whenever the Qiang and Hu raided the passes Rong always led in person with the commanderies to the rescue, every move matched the plan, and each time he routed them.

sentences.zh: 其後羌、胡皆震服親附，內郡流民避凶饑者歸之不絕。

translations.literal: Afterward Qiang and Hu were all awed into submission and drew near; refugees from inner commanderies fleeing disaster and famine came to them without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the Qiang and Hu were all awed into submission and drew near, and refugees from the inner commanderies fleeing disaster and famine came to them without cease.

sentences.zh: 25王莽之世，天下咸思漢德，安定三水盧芳居左谷中，詐稱武帝曾孫劉文伯，云「曾祖母，匈奴渾邪王之姊也」。

translations.literal: 25. In Wang Mang's age the realm all longed for Han's virtue; Anding's Sanshui Lu Fang dwelt in Zuogu valley, falsely styled himself Emperor Wu's great-grandson Liu Wenbo, saying "My great-grandmother was sister to the Xiongnu King who Surrendered with Good Faith."
translations.idiomatic: 25. In Wang Mang's age the realm all longed for Han's virtue; Lu Fang of Sanshui in Anding dwelt in Zuogu valley, falsely styled himself Emperor Wu's great-grandson Liu Wenbo, and said, "My great-grandmother was sister to the Xiongnu King who Surrendered with Good Faith."

sentences.zh: 常以是言誑惑安定間。

translations.literal: He constantly used this speech to deceive those in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly used this tale to deceive the people of Anding.

sentences.zh: 王莽末，乃與三水屬國羌、胡起兵。

translations.literal: At Wang Mang's end he then with Sanshui dependent state's Qiang and Hu raised troops.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wang Mang's reign he raised troops with the Qiang and Hu of the Sanshui dependent state.

sentences.zh: 更始至長安，征芳為騎都尉，使鎮撫安定以西。

translations.literal: When Gengshi reached Chang'an he summoned Fang as Cavalry Commandant and sent him to pacify Anding and west.
translations.idiomatic: When Gengshi reached Chang'an he summoned Fang as Cavalry Commandant and sent him to pacify Anding and the region west of it.

sentences.zh: 更始敗，三水豪桀共立芳為上將軍、西平王，使使與西羌、匈奴結和親。

translations.literal: When Gengshi fell, Sanshui's bold leaders together enthroned Fang as Grand General and King Who Pacifies the West, and sent envoys to ally in marriage with Western Qiang and the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: When Gengshi fell, the bold leaders of Sanshui together enthroned Fang as Grand General and King Who Pacifies the West and sent envoys to ally in marriage with the Western Qiang and the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 單于以為：「漢氏中絕，劉氏來歸，我亦當如呼韓邪立之，令尊事我。

translations.literal: The chanyu thought: "Han is cut off in the middle; the Liu house has come to submit—I too should establish him as with Huhanye, and have him honor and serve me.
translations.idiomatic: The chanyu thought, "Han is cut off in the middle; the Liu house has come to submit—I too should establish him as I did Huhanye and have him honor and serve me."

sentences.zh: 」乃使句林王將數千騎迎芳兄弟入匈奴，立芳為漢帝，以芳弟程為中郎將，將胡騎還入安定。

translations.literal: " He then sent the King of Goulin with several thousand horsemen to welcome Fang and his brothers into the Xiongnu, enthroned Fang as Han Emperor, made Fang's younger brother Cheng Central Palace Gentleman, and led Hu cavalry back into Anding.
translations.idiomatic: " He then sent the King of Goulin with several thousand horsemen to welcome Fang and his brothers into the Xiongnu, enthroned Fang as Han Emperor, made Fang's younger brother Cheng Central Palace Gentleman, and led Xiongnu cavalry back into Anding.

sentences.zh: 26帝以關中未定，而鄧禹久不進兵，賜書責之曰：「司徒，堯也；

translations.literal: 26. The Emperor because Guanzhong was not settled and Deng Yu long did not advance troops, granted a letter reproaching him: "Minister of the Masses is Yao;
translations.idiomatic: 26. Because Guanzhong was not yet settled and Deng Yu had long failed to advance, the Emperor sent him a letter of reproach, saying, "The Minister of the Masses is Yao;

sentences.zh: 亡賊，桀也。

translations.literal: the perished bandits are Jie.
translations.idiomatic: the doomed bandits are Jie.

sentences.zh: 長安吏民遑遑無所依歸，宜以時進討，鎮慰西京，繫百姓之心。

translations.literal: Chang'an's officials and people are anxious with nowhere to rely—you should advance and campaign in season, pacify and comfort the western capital, and bind the hundred surnames' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Chang'an's officials and people are anxious with nowhere to turn; you should advance and campaign in season, pacify and comfort the western capital, and bind the people's hearts."

sentences.zh: 」禹猶執前意，別攻上郡諸縣，更徵兵引穀，歸至大要。

translations.literal: " Yu still held to his former intent, separately attacked Shang commandery's counties, again levied troops and drew grain, and returned to Dayao.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu still held to his former plan, separately attacked the counties of Shang commandery, again levied troops and drew grain, and returned to Dayao.

sentences.zh: 積弩將軍馮愔、車騎將軍宗歆守栒邑，二人爭權相攻，愔遂殺歆，因反擊禹，禹遣使以聞。

translations.literal: Stacked-crossbow General Feng Yin and Chariots-and-Cavalry General Zong Xin guarded Xunyi; the two contended for power and attacked each other—Yin then killed Xin and turned to strike Yu; Yu sent an envoy to report.
translations.idiomatic: Stacked-Crossbow General Feng Yin and Chariots-and-Cavalry General Zong Xin guarded Xunyi; the two fought over power, Yin killed Xin, and turned to strike Yu; Yu sent an envoy to report it.

sentences.zh: 帝問使人：「愔所親愛為誰？

translations.literal: The Emperor asked the envoy: "Whom does Yin love and favor?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked the envoy, "Whom does Yin love and favor?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「護軍黃防。

translations.literal: " He answered: "Protector of the Army Huang Fang."
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "Protector of the Army Huang Fang."

sentences.zh: 」帝度愔、防不能久和，勢必相忤，因報禹曰：「縛馮愔者，必黃防也。

translations.literal: " The Emperor reckoned Yin and Fang could not long be at peace and would surely clash, and therefore replied to Yu: "Whoever binds Feng Yin will surely be Huang Fang."
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor reckoned Yin and Fang could not long remain at peace and would surely clash, and therefore replied to Yu, "Whoever binds Feng Yin will surely be Huang Fang."

sentences.zh: 」乃遣尚書宗廣持節往降之。

translations.literal: " He then sent Masters of Writing Zong Guang bearing credentials to go and accept their surrender.
translations.idiomatic: " He then sent Masters of Writing Zong Guang bearing credentials to go and accept their surrender.

sentences.zh: 後月餘，防果執愔，將其眾歸罪。

translations.literal: More than a month later Fang indeed seized Yin and led his host back to answer for the crime.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month later Fang indeed seized Yin and led his troops back to answer for the crime.

sentences.zh: 更始諸將王匡、胡殷、成丹等皆詣廣降，廣與東歸；

translations.literal: Gengshi's generals Wang Kuang, Hu Yin, Cheng Dan and others all came to Guang to surrender; Guang went east with them;
translations.idiomatic: Gengshi's generals Wang Kuang, Hu Yin, Cheng Dan, and others all came to Guang to surrender, and Guang went east with them;

sentences.zh: 至安邑，道欲亡，廣悉斬之。

translations.literal: reaching Anyi, on the road they wished to flee—Guang beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: at Anyi they wished to flee on the road, and Guang beheaded them all.

sentences.zh: 愔之叛也，引兵西向天水；

translations.literal: When Yin rebelled he led troops west toward Tianshui;
translations.idiomatic: When Yin rebelled he led troops west toward Tianshui;

sentences.zh: 隗囂逆擊，破之於高平，盡獲其輜重。

translations.literal: Wei Xiao met and struck him, broke him at Gaoping, and took all his baggage train.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiao met and struck him, routed him at Gaoping, and took all his baggage train.

sentences.zh: 於是禹承製遣使持節命囂為西州大將軍，得專制涼州、朔方事。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yu, acting on the imperial edict, sent an envoy bearing credentials to appoint Xiao Western Province Grand General, with full discretion over Liang and Shuofang affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yu, acting on the imperial edict, sent an envoy bearing credentials to appoint Xiao Western Province Grand General with full discretion over Liang and Shuofang affairs.

sentences.zh: 27臘日，赤眉設樂大會，酒未行，群臣更相辯斗；

translations.literal: 27. On the La festival day the Red Eyebrows set music for a great assembly—before the wine was served the ministers argued and fought one another;
translations.idiomatic: 27. On the La festival day the Red Eyebrows set music for a great assembly; before the wine was served the ministers argued and fought one another;

sentences.zh: 而兵眾遂各逾宮，斬關入，掠酒肉，互相殺傷。

translations.literal: then the soldiers each crossed the palaces, cut the gates and entered, plundered wine and meat, and killed and wounded one another.
translations.idiomatic: then the soldiers each stormed the palaces, cut through the gates, plundered wine and meat, and killed and wounded one another.

sentences.zh: 衛尉諸葛稚聞之，勒兵入，格殺百餘人，乃定。

translations.literal: Commandant of the Guard Zhuge Zhi heard it, drew troops in, and killed more than a hundred in the melee—then it was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of the Guard Zhuge Zhi heard of it, drew troops in, and killed more than a hundred in the melee before order was restored.

sentences.zh: 劉盆子惶恐，日夜啼泣，從官皆憐之。

translations.literal: Liu Penzi was terrified, weeping day and night; his attendants all pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Penzi was terrified and wept day and night; his attendants all pitied him.

sentences.zh: 28帝遣宗正劉延攻天井關，與田邑連戰十餘合，延不得進。

translations.literal: 28. The Emperor sent Director of the Imperial Clan Liu Yan to attack Tianjing Pass; with Tian Yi he fought more than ten engagements in succession—Yan could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: 28. The Emperor sent Director of the Imperial Clan Liu Yan to attack Tianjing Pass; he fought more than ten engagements in succession with Tian Yi and could not advance.

sentences.zh: 及更始敗，邑遣使請降；

translations.literal: When Gengshi fell, Yi sent an envoy to request surrender;
translations.idiomatic: When Gengshi fell, Yi sent an envoy to request surrender;

sentences.zh: 即拜為上黨太守。

translations.literal: he was at once appointed Shangdang Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: he was at once appointed Shangdang Administrator.

sentences.zh: 帝又遣諫議大夫儲大伯持節徵鮑永；

translations.literal: The Emperor also sent Remonstrance Grandee Chu Dabo bearing credentials to summon Bao Yong;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor also sent Remonstrance Grandee Chu Dabo bearing credentials to summon Bao Yong;

sentences.zh: 永未知更始存亡，疑不肯從，收繫大伯，遣使馳至長安，詗問虛實。

translations.literal: Yong did not know whether Gengshi lived or perished, suspected and would not follow—he seized and bound Dabo, sent an envoy galloping to Chang'an to inquire the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Yong did not know whether Gengshi still lived, suspected the summons, and refused to obey; he seized and bound Dabo and sent an envoy galloping to Chang'an to learn the truth.

sentences.zh: 29初，帝從更始在宛，納新野陰氏之女麗華。

translations.literal: 29. At first, when the Emperor followed Gengshi at Wan, he took as wife Xinye's Lady Yin Lihua.
translations.idiomatic: 29. At first, when the Emperor followed Gengshi at Wan, he took as wife Lady Yin Lihua of the Yin clan of Xinye.

sentences.zh: 是歲，遣使迎麗華與帝姊湖陽公主、妹寧平公主俱到洛陽；

translations.literal: That year he sent an envoy to welcome Lihua, the Emperor's elder sister the Princess of Huyang, and his younger sister the Princess of Ningping—all together to Luoyang;
translations.idiomatic: That year he sent an envoy to welcome Lihua, the Emperor's elder sister the Princess of Huyang, and his younger sister the Princess of Ningping, all together to Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 以麗華為貴人。

translations.literal: he made Lihua Honored Lady.
translations.idiomatic: he made Lihua Honored Lady.

sentences.zh: 更始西平王李通先娶寧平公主，上征通為衛尉。

translations.literal: Gengshi's King Who Pacifies the West Li Tong had earlier married the Princess of Ningping; the Emperor summoned Tong as Commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Gengshi's King Who Pacifies the West, Li Tong, had earlier married the Princess of Ningping; the Emperor summoned Tong as Commandant of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 30初，更始以王閎為琅邪太守，張步據郡拒之。

translations.literal: 30. At first Gengshi made Wang Hong Administrator of Langye; Zhang Bu held the commandery and refused him.
translations.idiomatic: 30. At first Gengshi made Wang Hong Administrator of Langye; Zhang Bu held the commandery and refused him.

sentences.zh: 閎諭降，得贛榆等六縣；

translations.literal: Hong persuaded surrender and got Gan Yu and six other counties;
translations.idiomatic: Hong persuaded men to surrender and took Gan Yu and six other counties;

sentences.zh: 收兵與步戰，不勝。

translations.literal: he gathered troops and fought Bu—could not win.
translations.idiomatic: he gathered troops and fought Bu but could not win.

sentences.zh: 步既受劉永官號，治兵於劇，遣將徇泰山、東萊、城陽、膠東、北海、濟南、齊郡，皆下之。

translations.literal: Bu having received Liu Yong's titles and offices, drilled troops at Ju, sent generals to overrun Taishan, Donglai, Chengyang, Jiaodong, Beihai, Jinan, and Qi commanderies—all were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Bu, having received Liu Yong's titles and offices, drilled troops at Ju and sent generals to overrun Taishan, Donglai, Chengyang, Jiaodong, Beihai, Jinan, and Qi commandery; all submitted.

sentences.zh: 閎力不敵，乃詣步相見。

translations.literal: Hong's strength could not match him, so he went to Bu to meet face to face.
translations.idiomatic: Hong could not match his strength and went to meet Bu in person.

sentences.zh: 步大陳兵而見之。

translations.literal: Bu arrayed troops in great force to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: Bu arrayed a great force of troops to receive him.

sentences.zh: 怒曰：「步有何罪，君前見攻之甚！

translations.literal: Angry, he said: "What crime has Bu committed, that you earlier attacked me so fiercely!
translations.idiomatic: Angry, he said, "What crime has Bu committed, that you earlier attacked me so fiercely!

sentences.zh: 」閎按劍曰：「太守奉朝命，而文公擁兵相拒。

translations.literal: " Hong gripped his sword and said: "The Administrator obeys the court's command, while Lord Wen holds troops and resists.
translations.idiomatic: " Hong gripped his sword and said, "The Administrator obeys the court's command, while Lord Wen holds troops and resists.

sentences.zh: 閎攻賊耳，何謂甚邪！

translations.literal: Hong attacks bandits—what do you call fierce!
translations.idiomatic: Hong attacks bandits—what do you call fierce!"

sentences.zh: 」步起跪謝，與之宴飲，待為上賓，令閎關掌郡事。

translations.literal: " Bu rose and knelt in apology, feasted and drank with him, treated him as a chief guest, and ordered Hong to oversee the commandery's affairs at the passes.
translations.idiomatic: " Bu rose and knelt in apology, feasted with him, treated him as a chief guest, and put Hong in charge of the commandery's affairs at the passes.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，甲子朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: 1. Spring, first month, on the first day jiazi there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In spring, the first month, on the first day jiazi there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 2劉恭知赤眉必敗，密教弟盆子歸璽綬，習為辭讓之言。

translations.literal: 2. Liu Gong knew the Red Eyebrows would surely fall; he secretly taught his younger brother Penzi to return seal and cord and practiced words of yielding.
translations.idiomatic: 2. Liu Gong knew the Red Eyebrows would surely fall; he secretly taught his younger brother Penzi to return the seal and cord and practiced words of yielding.

sentences.zh: 及正旦大會，恭先曰：「諸君共立恭弟為帝，德誠深厚！

translations.literal: At the New Year's great assembly Gong spoke first: "You gentlemen together enthroned Gong's younger brother as emperor—your virtue is truly deep and thick!
translations.idiomatic: At the New Year's great assembly Gong spoke first, "You gentlemen together enthroned my younger brother as emperor—your virtue is truly deep and great!

sentences.zh: 立且一年，殽亂日甚，誠不足以相成，恐死而無益，願得退為庶人，更求賢知，唯諸君省察！

translations.literal: Enthroned nearly a year, chaos grows worse daily—truly not enough to accomplish together; I fear to die without benefit. I wish to withdraw and become a common man, and seek the worthy and wise anew—only let you gentlemen reflect!
translations.idiomatic: He has reigned nearly a year, yet chaos grows worse daily—truly we cannot accomplish anything together, and I fear to die without benefit. I wish to withdraw and become a common man and seek the worthy and wise anew—only let you gentlemen reflect!"

sentences.zh: 」樊崇等謝曰：「此者崇等罪也。

translations.literal: " Fan Chong and others apologized: "This is Chong and others' crime.
translations.idiomatic: " Fan Chong and others apologized, "This is Chong and others' crime."

sentences.zh: 」恭復固請，或曰：「此寧式侯事邪？

translations.literal: " Gong again firmly requested; some said: "Is this surely the Marquis of Shi's affair?
translations.idiomatic: " Gong again firmly requested; some said, "Is this surely the Marquis of Shi's affair?"

sentences.zh: 」恭惶恐起去。

translations.literal: " Gong in terror rose and left.
translations.idiomatic: " Gong rose in terror and left.

sentences.zh: 盆子乃下床解璽綬，叩頭曰：「今設置縣官而為賊如故，四方怨恨，不覆信向，此皆立非其人所致。

translations.literal: Penzi then came down from the bed, unfastened seal and cord, kowtowed and said: "Now we set up county officials yet act as bandits as before—the four quarters resent it and will not again trust and turn to us; all this comes from enthroning the wrong man.
translations.idiomatic: Penzi then came down from the bed, unfastened the seal and cord, kowtowed, and said, "Now we set up county officials yet act as bandits as before—the four quarters resent us and will not trust us again; all this comes from enthroning the wrong man.

sentences.zh: 願乞骸骨，避賢聖路！

translations.literal: I beg to offer my bones and withdraw, clearing the road for the worthy and sage!
translations.idiomatic: I beg to offer my bones and withdraw, clearing the road for the worthy and sage!

sentences.zh: 必欲殺盆子以塞責者，無所離死！

translations.literal: If you must kill Penzi to answer for the blame, I have nowhere to flee from death!
translations.idiomatic: If you must kill Penzi to answer for the blame, I have nowhere to flee from death!"

sentences.zh: 」因涕泣噓唏。

translations.literal: " He then wept and sobbed.
translations.idiomatic: " He then wept and sobbed.

sentences.zh: 崇等及會者數百人，莫不哀憐之，乃皆避席頓首曰：「臣無狀，負陛下，請自今已後，不敢復放縱！

translations.literal: Chong and others and those at the assembly, several hundred, none did not pity him in sorrow; they all left their mats and knocked their heads, saying: "Your subjects are without form, we have failed Your Majesty—from now on we dare not again run wild!
translations.idiomatic: Chong and the several hundred at the assembly all pitied him; they left their mats and knocked their heads, saying, "Your subjects have failed Your Majesty—from now on we dare not run wild again!"

sentences.zh: 」因共抱持盆子，帶以璽綬；

translations.literal: " They then together embraced and held Penzi, belted him with seal and cord;
translations.idiomatic: " They then together embraced Penzi and belted him with the seal and cord;

sentences.zh: 盆子號呼，不得已。

translations.literal: Penzi cried out—he could not help it.
translations.idiomatic: Penzi cried out, unable to refuse.

sentences.zh: 既罷出，各閉營自守。

translations.literal: When the assembly ended and they went out, each closed camp and held himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the assembly ended they went out, and each closed his camp and held to himself.

sentences.zh: 三輔翕然，稱天子聰明，百姓爭還長安，市裡且滿。

translations.literal: The three adjuncts were united in praise, calling the Son of Heaven clear-sighted; the hundred surnames vied to return to Chang'an, and the markets were nearly full.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Adjuncts united in praise, calling the Son of Heaven clear-sighted; the people vied to return to Chang'an until the markets were nearly full.

sentences.zh: 後二十餘日，復出，大掠如故。

translations.literal: After more than twenty days they again went out and plundered on a great scale as before.
translations.idiomatic: After more than twenty days they again went out and plundered on a great scale as before.

translations.idiomatic: 3. [Diao](

translations.idiomatic: Dao)

translations.literal: Zi Du was killed by his own retainers<ref>[Diao](

translations.literal: Dao)

translations.idiomatic: He also sent Liang with Grand General Du Mao to lead troops and pacify Wei, Qinghe, and Dong commanderies, leveling all fortified camps; the three commanderies were clear and quiet and the border roads were open.

translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Liang Deng Yu and Marquis of Guangping Wu Han each drew revenue from four counties.

translations.idiomatic: Erudite Ding Gong remonstrated, "In antiquity enfeoffing feudal lords did not exceed a hundred li—strengthening the trunk and weakening the branches was how to govern.

translations.idiomatic: Now enfeoffing four counties does not accord with law and regulation."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「古之亡國皆以無道，未嘗聞功臣地多而滅亡者也。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "States of antiquity that perished all did so through lack of the Way—I have never heard of a merit minister perishing because his lands were many.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said, "States of antiquity that perished all did so through lack of the Way—I have never heard of a merit minister perishing because his lands were many."

translations.literal: " Yinxiang Marquis Yin Shi, the Honored Lady's elder brother, by military merit ought to have his enfeoffment increased; Shi knocked his head and declined: "The realm is newly settled—generals with merit are many; your subject relies on the palace harem and still receives added rank and fief—this cannot be shown to the realm.

translations.idiomatic: Ding Shen of Yingchuan, Grand Administrator of Henan, alone requested enfeoffment in his native district.

sentences.zh: 或問其故，綝曰：「綝能薄功微，得鄉亭厚矣！

translations.idiomatic: The Emperor followed his wish and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Xin'an district.

translations.idiomatic: The Emperor considered him capable and ordered him to oversee and record all Masters of Writing business.

translations.idiomatic: Chun reached Zhending, stopped at the relay lodge, and invited Yang to meet.

translations.idiomatic: Yang entered and saw Chun; Chun received him with courtesy, then invited his brothers in as well; he shut the gate passage, executed them all, and led his troops out.

sentences.zh: 真定震怖，無敢動者。

translations.literal: Zhending was shaken in terror; none dared move.
translations.idiomatic: Zhending was shaken with terror; none dared stir.

sentences.zh: 帝憐楊謀未發而誅，復封其子為真定王。

translations.idiomatic: The Emperor pitied that Yang had been executed before his plot erupted, and again enfeoffed his son as Prince of Zhending.

translations.idiomatic: But he was not pleased.

translations.literal: now encountering a bright lord—what is there to worry about!
translations.idiomatic: now that we have met a bright lord, what is there to worry about!"

sentences.zh: 」衍曰：「人有挑其鄰人之妻者，其長者罵而少者報之。

translations.idiomatic: Yan said, "A man flirted with his neighbor's wife; the elder rebuked him while the younger repaid her favors.

translations.idiomatic: Later, when her husband died, she married the elder man.

translations.idiomatic: Someone said to her, 'Was not your husband the one who scolded you?'

translations.idiomatic: She said, 'When I was another man's wife I wanted him to repay me; as my own wife I wanted him to scold others!'

sentences.zh: 』夫天命難知，人道易守，守道之臣，何患死亡！

translations.literal: ' Heaven's mandate is hard to know; the human Way is easy to keep—a minister who keeps the Way—what fear of death or ruin!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's mandate is hard to know, but the human Way is easy to keep. For a minister who keeps the Way, what fear of death or ruin!"

translations.idiomatic: 10 Grand Minister of Works Wang Liang repeatedly disobeyed imperial orders; the Emperor was angry and dispatched Master of Writing Zong Guang bearing credentials to behead Liang in the army;

translations.idiomatic: 12 When the Emperor was attacking Wang Lang, Peng Chong sent shock cavalry to aid the army and transported grain without cease; when the Emperor pursued the Bronze Horses to Ji, Chong relied on his merit and his expectations were very high;

translations.idiomatic: As it is, has Your Majesty forgotten me!"

translations.idiomatic: At this time the northern provinces were broken and scattered, while Yuyang was comparatively intact; it had an old iron office, and Chong traded grain, amassed treasures, and grew ever wealthier and stronger.

sentences.zh: 幽州牧朱浮，年少有俊才，欲厲風跡，收士心，辟召州中名宿及王莽時故吏二千石，皆引置幕府，多發諸郡倉穀稟贍其妻子。

translations.literal: Youzhou Regional Governor Zhu Fu, young and possessing outstanding talent, wished to sharpen conduct and reputation and win scholars' hearts; he summoned renowned elders of the province and former Mang-era officials at the two-thousand-bushel level, all placing them in his headquarters, and issued much from the various commanderies' granaries to provision their wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou Regional Governor Zhu Fu, young and talented, wished to sharpen his reputation and win scholars' hearts; he summoned renowned elders of the province and former Wang Mang-era officials at the two-thousand-bushel level, placed them all in his headquarters, and drew heavily from commandery granaries to provision their wives and children.

sentences.zh: 寵以為天下未定，師旅方起，不宜多置官屬以損軍實，不從其令。

translations.idiomatic: Chong thought the realm was not yet settled and armies were just rising—it was inappropriate to place many officials and thereby drain military resources—and he did not obey Fu's orders.

sentences.zh: 浮性矜急自多，寵亦狠強，嫌怨轉積。

translations.literal: Fu was by nature proud, hasty, and self-important; Chong was also fierce and strong—and mutual resentment accumulated.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was proud, hasty, and self-important; Chong was also fierce and strong, and their mutual resentment grew.

sentences.zh: 浮數譖構之，密奏寵多聚兵穀，意計難量。

translations.literal: Fu repeatedly slandered and framed him, secretly memorializing that Chong had amassed much troops and grain and his intent was hard to measure.
translations.idiomatic: Fu repeatedly slandered him and secretly memorialized that Chong had amassed troops and grain and his intentions were hard to gauge.

sentences.zh: 上輒漏泄令寵聞，以脅恐之。

translations.idiomatic: The sovereign repeatedly leaked word for Chong to hear, to intimidate him.

translations.idiomatic: the Emperor did not permit it.

translations.literal: Chong grew the more self-suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Chong grew ever more suspicious.

sentences.zh: 其妻素剛，不堪抑屈，固勸無受徵，曰：「天下未定，四方各自為雄。

translations.literal: His wife was by nature fierce, could not bear restraint, and firmly urged him not to accept the summons, saying: "All under Heaven is not settled; the four quarters each make themselves hegemons.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was fierce by nature and could not bear restraint; she firmly urged him not to accept the summons, saying, "The realm is not settled; each quarter has its own champion.

translations.idiomatic: If trouble arises suddenly, I am enough to match him."

translations.idiomatic: He thereupon ordered the subordinate counties to prepare abundant supplies, store wine, and when the Bearer of the Mace's army entered the border, each man was served a feast for two.

translations.literal: Xun went out to meet him on the road, claimed illness, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Xun went out to meet him on the road, claimed illness, and returned.

sentences.zh: 復勒兵欲追之，而吏士皆醉，遂過去。

translations.literal: Fu reined his troops wanting to pursue, but the officers and soldiers were all drunk, so he passed on.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Fu reined his troops wanting to pursue, but the officers and soldiers were all drunk, so he passed on.

translations.idiomatic: Kou Xun sent Gu Chong to report the situation; the emperor thereupon summoned Kou Xun.

translations.literal: When Xun arrived, he was granted audience;
translations.idiomatic: When Kou Xun arrived, he was granted audience;

sentences.zh: 時賈復先在坐，欲起相避。

translations.literal: at the time Jia Fu was already seated and wished to rise to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: at the time Jia Fu was already seated and wished to rise to avoid him.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「天下未定，兩虎安得私鬥！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The realm is not yet settled—how can two tigers fight in private!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The realm is not yet settled—how can two tigers fight in private!"

sentences.zh: 今日朕分之。

translations.literal: Today I divide between you.
translations.idiomatic: Today I divide between you."

sentences.zh: 」於是並坐極歡，遂共車同出，結友而去。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they sat together in greatest pleasure, then rode out in the same carriage, became friends, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they sat together in greatest pleasure, then rode out in the same carriage, became friends, and departed.

sentences.zh: 24八月，帝自率諸將征五校。

translations.literal: 24. Eighth month, the emperor himself led the generals in campaign against the Five Banners.
translations.idiomatic: 24. In the eighth month, the emperor himself led the generals in campaign against the Five Banners.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，幸內黃，大破五校於羛陽，降其眾五萬人。

translations.literal: On bingchen, he arrived at Neihuang and greatly routed the Five Banners at Yang, accepting the surrender of fifty thousand of their masses.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, he arrived at Neihuang and greatly routed the Five Banners at Yang, accepting the surrender of fifty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 25帝遣游擊將軍鄧隆助朱浮討彭寵。

translations.literal: 25. The emperor sent Mobile-Camp General Deng Long to assist Zhu Fu in attacking Peng Chong.
translations.idiomatic: 25. The emperor sent Mobile-Camp General Deng Long to assist Zhu Fu in attacking Peng Chong.

sentences.zh: 隆軍潞南，浮軍雍奴，遣吏奏狀。

translations.literal: Long's army at Lunan, Fu's army at Yongnu, they sent clerks to memorialize the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Long's army was at Lunan and Zhu Fu's at Yongnu; they sent clerks to memorialize the situation.

sentences.zh: 帝讀檄，怒，謂使吏曰：「營相去百里，其勢豈可得相及！

translations.literal: The emperor read the dispatch, was angry, and said to the envoy clerk: "The camps are a hundred li apart—how could their forces possibly aid each other!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the dispatch, was angry, and said to the envoy clerk, "The camps are a hundred li apart—how could their forces possibly aid each other!"

sentences.zh: 比若還，北軍必敗矣。

translations.literal: By the time they return, the northern army is sure to be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they return, the northern army is sure to be defeated."

sentences.zh: 」彭寵果遣輕兵擊隆軍，大破之；

translations.literal: " Peng Chong indeed sent light troops to strike Long's army and greatly defeated them;
translations.idiomatic: Peng Chong indeed sent light troops to strike Deng Long's army and routed them;

sentences.zh: 浮遠，遂不能救。

translations.literal: Fu was far away and could not rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Fu was far away and could not rescue.

sentences.zh: 26蓋延圍睢陽數月，克之。

translations.literal: 26. Gai Yan besieged Suiyang for several months and took it.
translations.idiomatic: 26. Gai Yan besieged Suiyang for several months and took it.

sentences.zh: 劉永走至虞，虞人反，殺其母、妻；

translations.literal: Liu Yong fled to Yu; the people of Yu rebelled and killed his mother and wife;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yong fled to Yu; the people of Yu rebelled and killed his mother and wife;

sentences.zh: 永與麾下數十人奔譙。

translations.literal: Yong with several tens of his personal followers fled to Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yong with several tens of his personal followers fled to Qiao.

sentences.zh: 蘇茂、佼彊、周建合軍三萬餘人救永；

translations.literal: Su Mao, Jiao Qiang, and Zhou Jian united armies of more than thirty thousand to rescue Yong;
translations.idiomatic: Su Mao, Jiao Qiang, and Zhou Jian united armies of more than thirty thousand to rescue Liu Yong;

sentences.zh: 延與戰於沛西，大破之。

translations.literal: Yan battled them west of Pei and routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Gai Yan battled them west of Pei and routed them greatly.

sentences.zh: 永、彊、建走保湖陵，茂奔還廣樂；

translations.literal: Yong, Qiang, and Jian fled to hold Huling; Mao fled back to Guangle;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yong, Jiao Qiang, and Zhou Jian fled to hold Huling; Su Mao fled back to Guangle;

sentences.zh: 延遂定沛、楚、臨淮。

translations.literal: Yan thereupon pacified Pei, Chu, and Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Gai Yan thereupon pacified Pei, Chu, and Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 帝使太中大夫伏隆持節使青、徐二州，招降郡國。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Palace Counsellor Fu Long bearing credentials as envoy to Qing and Xu two provinces to summon and receive the surrender of commanderies and states.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Palace Counsellor Fu Long bearing credentials as envoy to Qing and Xu to summon and receive the surrender of commanderies and states.

sentences.zh: 青、徐群盜聞劉永破敗，皆惶怖請降。

translations.literal: Bandits in Qing and Xu, hearing Liu Yong was defeated, were all fearful and begged to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits in Qing and Xu, hearing Liu Yong was defeated, were all fearful and begged to submit.

sentences.zh: 張步遣其掾孫昱隨隆詣闕上書，獻鰒魚。

translations.literal: Zhang Bu sent his clerk Sun Yu to follow Long to the capital to present a memorial and offer preserved fish.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bu sent his clerk Sun Yu to follow Fu Long to the capital to present a memorial and offer preserved fish.

sentences.zh: 隆，湛之子也。

translations.literal: Long was son of Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Long was the son of Fu Zhan.

sentences.zh: 27堵鄉人董訢反宛城，執南陽太守劉驎。

translations.literal: 27. Dong Xin of Duxiang rebelled at Wancheng and seized Administrator of Nanyang Liu Lin.
translations.idiomatic: 27. Dong Xin of Duxiang rebelled at Wancheng and seized Administrator of Nanyang Liu Lin.

sentences.zh: 揚化將軍堅鐔攻宛，拔之；

translations.literal: Exaltation General Jian Tan attacked Wan and took it;
translations.idiomatic: Exaltation General Jian Tan attacked Wan and took it;

sentences.zh: 訢走還堵鄉。

translations.literal: Xin fled back to Duxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Xin fled back to Duxiang.

sentences.zh: 28吳漢徇南陽諸縣，所過多侵暴。

translations.literal: 28. Wu Han overrun Nanyang's various counties; wherever he passed he largely plundered violently.
translations.idiomatic: 28. Wu Han overran Nanyang's various counties; wherever he passed he largely plundered violently.

sentences.zh: 破虜將軍鄧奉謁歸新野，怒漢掠其鄉里，遂反，擊破漢軍，屯據淯陽，與諸賊合從。

translations.literal: Overthrow-the-Barbarians General Deng Feng paid a visit returning to Xinye, was angry that Han had raided his home district, thereupon rebelled, struck and routed Han's army, encamped at Yuyang, and joined in alliance with the various bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Overthrow-the-Barbarians General Deng Feng paid a visit returning to Xinye, was angry that Wu Han had raided his home district, thereupon rebelled, struck and routed Wu Han's army, encamped at Yuyang, and joined in alliance with the various bandits.

sentences.zh: 29九月，壬戌，帝自內黃還。

translations.literal: 29. Ninth month, renxu, the emperor returned from Neihuang.
translations.idiomatic: 29. In the ninth month, on renxu, the emperor returned from Neihuang.

sentences.zh: 30陝賊蘇況攻破弘農，帝使景丹討之。

translations.literal: 30. Su Kuang the bandit of Shaan attacked and took Hongnong; the emperor sent Jing Dan to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: 30. Su Kuang the bandit of Shaan attacked and took Hongnong; the emperor sent Jing Dan to attack him.

sentences.zh: 會丹薨，征虜將軍祭遵擊弘農、柏華、蠻中賊，皆平之。

translations.literal: When Dan died, Campaign General Ji Zun attacked Hongnong, Baihua, and Manzhong bandits and pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing Dan died, Campaign General Ji Zun attacked the Hongnong, Baihua, and Manzhong bandits and pacified them all.

sentences.zh: 31赤眉引兵欲西上隴，隗囂遣將軍楊廣迎擊，破之；

translations.literal: 31. The Red Eyebrows led troops wishing to go west up the Long Road; Wei Ao sent General Yang Guang to meet and attack and routed them;
translations.idiomatic: 31. The Red Eyebrows led troops wishing to go west up the Long Road; Wei Ao sent General Yang Guang to meet and attack and routed them;

sentences.zh: 又追敗之於烏氏、涇陽間。

translations.literal: he again pursued and defeated them between Wushi and Jingyang.
translations.idiomatic: he again pursued and defeated them between Wushi and Jingyang.

sentences.zh: 赤眉至陽城番須中，逢大雪，坑谷皆滿，士多凍死。

translations.literal: The Red Eyebrows reached Yangcheng in the Fanxu region; they met great snow, gullies and ravines were all full, and many soldiers froze to death.
translations.idiomatic: The Red Eyebrows reached Yangcheng in the Fanxu region; they met great snow, gullies and ravines were all full, and many soldiers froze to death.

sentences.zh: 乃復還，發掘諸陵，取其寶貨。

translations.literal: They thereupon returned again, dug open the various tombs, and took their treasures.
translations.idiomatic: They thereupon returned again, dug open the various tombs, and took their treasures.

sentences.zh: 凡有玉匣殮者，率皆如生，賊遂污辱呂后尸。

translations.literal: Wherever there were jade casket burials, all were as if alive; the bandits thereupon violated and shamed Empress Lü's corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever there were jade-casket burials, the corpses were all as if alive; the bandits thereupon violated and shamed Empress Lü's corpse.

sentences.zh: 鄧禹遣兵擊之於郁夷，反為所敗。

translations.literal: Deng Yu sent troops to strike them at Yuyi and in turn was defeated by them.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yu sent troops to strike them at Yuyi and in turn was defeated by them.

sentences.zh: 禹乃出之雲陽。

translations.literal: Yu thereupon withdrew to Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yu thereupon withdrew to Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 赤眉復入長安。

translations.literal: The Red Eyebrows again entered Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: The Red Eyebrows again entered Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 延岑屯杜陵，赤眉將逢安擊之。

translations.literal: Yan Cen encamped at Duling; Red Eyebrows' general Feng An attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Cen encamped at Duling; Red Eyebrows' general Feng An attacked him.

sentences.zh: 鄧禹以安精兵在外，引兵襲長安；

translations.literal: Deng Yu, because An's crack troops were abroad, led troops to raid Chang'an;
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yu, because Feng An's crack troops were abroad, led troops to raid Chang'an;

sentences.zh: 會謝祿救至，禹兵敗走。

translations.literal: when Xie Lu's rescue arrived, Yu's army was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: when Xie Lu's rescue arrived, Deng Yu's army was defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 延岑擊逢安，大破之，死者十餘萬人。

translations.literal: Yan Cen attacked Feng An and routed him greatly; more than a hundred thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Cen attacked Feng An and routed him greatly; more than a hundred thousand died.

sentences.zh: 廖湛將赤眉十八萬攻漢中王嘉；

translations.literal: Liao Zhan led one hundred eighty thousand Red Eyebrows to attack King of Hanzhong Wang Jia;
translations.idiomatic: Liao Zhan led one hundred eighty thousand Red Eyebrows to attack King of Hanzhong Wang Jia;

sentences.zh: 嘉與戰於谷口，大破之，嘉手殺湛，遂到雲陽就穀。

translations.literal: Jia battled them at Gukou, routed them greatly; Jia personally killed Zhan, then went to Yunyang to obtain grain.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jia battled them at Gukou and routed them greatly; Jia personally killed Liao Zhan, then went to Yunyang to obtain grain.

sentences.zh: 嘉妻兄新野來歙，帝之姑子也。

translations.literal: Jia's wife's elder brother Laixi Lai Xin was the emperor's cousin by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jia's wife's elder brother Laixi Lai Xin was the emperor's cousin by marriage.

sentences.zh: 帝令鄧禹招嘉，嘉因歙詣禹降。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Deng Yu to summon Jia; Jia through Xin went to Yu and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Deng Yu to summon Wang Jia; Jia through Lai Xin went to Yu and submitted.

sentences.zh: 李寶倨慢，禹斬之。

translations.literal: Li Bao was arrogant and rude; Yu beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bao was arrogant and rude; Deng Yu beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 32冬，十一月，以廷尉岑彭為征南大將軍。

translations.literal: 32. Winter, eleventh month, the emperor made Censor-in-Chief Cen Peng Campaign-in-the-South Great General.
translations.idiomatic: 32. In winter, the eleventh month, the emperor made Censor-in-Chief Cen Peng Campaign-in-the-South Great General.

translations.literal: At a great assembly the Emperor pointed at Wang Chang and said to the assembled ministers: "This family led the generals of the lower Yangtze in assisting the Han house; their hearts are like metal and stone—a true loyal minister!
translations.idiomatic: At a great assembly the Emperor pointed at Wang Chang and said to the ministers, "This family led the generals of the lower Yangtze in assisting the Han house; their hearts are like metal and stone—a true loyal minister!"

translations.literal: " That same day he appointed Chang as Loyal-to-Han General and ordered him together with Cen Peng to lead Establish-the-Righteousness Grand General Zhu Hu and seven other generals to attack Deng Feng and Dong Xin.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he appointed Wang Chang Loyal-to-Han General and ordered him, with Cen Peng, to lead Establish-the-Righteousness Grand General Zhu Hu and seven other generals against Deng Feng and Dong Xin.

translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hu's army was defeated and he was captured by Deng Feng.

translations.literal: 33 The remnant bandits of Bronze Horse, Green Calf, and Youlai jointly set up Sun Deng as Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: 33 The remnant bandits of Bronze Horse, Green Calf, and Youlai jointly made Sun Deng Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 登將樂玄殺登，以其眾五萬餘人降。

translations.literal: Deng's general Yue Xuan killed Deng and surrendered with his masses of more than fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Deng's general Yue Xuan killed him and surrendered with more than fifty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 34鄧禹自馮愔叛後，威名稍損，又乏糧食，戰數不利，歸附者日益離散。

translations.literal: 34 After Deng Yu, since Feng Yin's rebellion, his prestige was somewhat diminished; he also lacked food; battles were repeatedly unfavorable; and those who had submitted daily dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: 34 After Feng Yin's rebellion, Deng Yu's prestige had faded somewhat; he also lacked provisions, battles went badly again and again, and those who had submitted drifted away day by day.

sentences.zh: 赤眉、延岑暴亂三輔，郡縣大姓各擁兵眾，禹不能定。

translations.literal: The Red Eyebrows and Yan Cen ravaged the Three Metropolises; great clans of commanderies and counties each held troops and masses—Yu could not pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: The Red Eyebrows and Yan Cen ravaged the Three Metropolises; great clans in every commandery and county held private armies, and Yu could not pacify the region.

translations.literal: The Emperor then sent Lieutenant General Feng Yi to replace Yu in attacking them; the imperial carriage escorted him to Henan and charged Yi, saying: "The Three Metropolises have suffered the disorders of Wang Mang and Gengshi, compounded by the atrocities of the Red Eyebrows and Yan Cen; the common folk are smeared with charcoal and have nowhere to appeal.

translations.literal: destroy their fortified camps and do not let them gather again.
translations.idiomatic: tear down their fortified camps and do not let them gather again.

translations.literal: Campaigning need not necessarily seize territory and slaughter cities—the essential is only to pacify and settle the people.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning need not seize territory and slaughter cities—the point is only to pacify and settle the people.

translations.literal: The generals are not unable to fight fiercely, yet they love plundering.
translations.idiomatic: The generals are not unable to fight, yet they love to plunder.

translations.literal: You by nature can control officers and soldiers—mind to discipline yourself and do not cause suffering to commanderies and counties!
translations.idiomatic: You by nature can control officers and soldiers—mind to discipline yourself and do not afflict the commanderies and counties!"

sentences.zh: 」異頓首受命，引而西，所至布威信，群盜多降。

translations.literal: " Feng Yi bowed his head, accepted the command, led forces westward; wherever he went he spread authority and trust, and many bandits surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yi bowed, accepted the charge, and led his army west; wherever he went he spread authority and trust, and many bandits surrendered.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：昔周人頌武王之德曰：「舖時繹思，我徂惟求定。

translations.literal: Your servant Guang says: Formerly the people of Zhou praised King Wu's virtue, saying: "Spread the time and prolong the thought; our going forth seeks only stability.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang remarks: Formerly the Zhou praised King Wu's virtue, saying, "Profound was his thoughtful care; our going forth sought only stability."

sentences.zh: 」言王者之兵志，在布陳威德安民而已。

translations.literal: " This states that the kingly army's aim is only to spread and display authority and virtue to settle the people.
translations.idiomatic: This means that the kingly army's aim is only to spread authority and virtue and settle the people.

sentences.zh: 觀光武之所以取關中，用是道也。

translations.literal: Observing how Guangwu took Guanzhong, he used this Way.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing how Guangwu took Guanzhong, he used this same Way.

sentences.zh: 豈不美哉！

translations.literal: Is it not beautiful!
translations.idiomatic: Is it not admirable!

sentences.zh: 35又詔徵鄧禹還，曰：「慎毋與窮寇爭鋒！

translations.literal: 35 Again he issued an edict summoning Deng Yu back, saying: "Take care not to contend with a cornered foe!
translations.idiomatic: 35 The Emperor again issued an edict summoning Deng Yu back, saying, "Take care not to fight a cornered foe!"

sentences.zh: 赤眉無穀，自當來東。

translations.literal: The Red Eyebrows have no grain—they will naturally come east.
translations.idiomatic: The Red Eyebrows have no grain—they will come east on their own.

sentences.zh: 吾以飽待饑，以逸待勞，折棰笞之，非諸將憂也。

translations.literal: We with full stomachs await the hungry, with ease await the weary—a broken whip will chastise them; this is not a worry for the generals.
translations.idiomatic: We with full bellies await the hungry, with ease await the weary—a broken whip will flog them—this is no worry for the generals.

sentences.zh: 無得復妄進兵！

translations.literal: Do not rashly advance troops again!
translations.idiomatic: Do not rashly advance troops again!"

sentences.zh: 帝以伏隆為光祿大夫，復使於張步，拜步東萊太守，并與新除青州牧、守、都尉俱東。

translations.literal: The Emperor made Fu Long Grand Master of Splendor and again sent him to Zhang Bu, appointing Bu Administrator of Donglai, and together with the newly appointed Governor of Qing Province, administrators, and commandants he went east together.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor made Fu Long Grand Master of Splendor and again sent him to Zhang Bu, appointing Bu Administrator of Donglai; together with the newly appointed governor of Qing Province and the administrators and commandants, they all went east.

sentences.zh: 詔隆輒拜令、長以下。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Long to appoint on the spot magistrates, chiefs, and those below.
translations.idiomatic: An edict authorized Long to appoint magistrates, chiefs, and subordinates on the spot.

sentences.zh: 36十二月，戊午，詔宗室列侯為王莽所絕者，皆復故國。

translations.literal: 36 In the twelfth month, on wuwu day, an edict: among collateral princes and marquises whose lines were extinguished by Wang Mang, all were restored to their former states.
translations.idiomatic: 36 In the twelfth month, on wuwu day, an edict restored to their former states all collateral princes and marquises whose lines Wang Mang had extinguished.

sentences.zh: 37三輔大饑，人相食，城郭皆空，白骨蔽野，遺民往往聚為營堡，各堅壁清野。

translations.literal: 37 The Three Metropolises suffered great famine; people ate one another; cities and ramparts were all empty; white bones covered the wilderness; surviving people often gathered into fortified camps, each securing walls and clearing the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: 37 The Three Metropolises suffered terrible famine; people ate one another; cities and towns stood empty; white bones covered the fields; survivors often gathered into fortified camps, each walling up and clearing the countryside.

sentences.zh: 赤眉虜掠無所得，乃引而東歸，眾尚二十餘萬，隨道復散。

translations.literal: The Red Eyebrows plundered but obtained nothing; they then led forces east in retreat—masses still more than two hundred thousand, scattering again along the road.
translations.idiomatic: The Red Eyebrows raided but gained nothing; they then marched east in retreat, still more than two hundred thousand strong, scattering again along the way.

sentences.zh: 帝遣破奸將軍侯進等屯新安，建威大將軍耿弇等屯宜陽，以要其還路，敕諸將曰：「賊若東走，可引宜陽兵會新安；

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Smash-Treason General Hou Jin and others to hold Xinan, Established-Power Grand General Geng Yin and others to hold Yiyang, to intercept their return route, charging the generals: "If the bandits flee east, you may draw the Yiyang troops to join at Xinan;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Smash-Treason General Hou Jin and others to hold Xinan and Established-Power Grand General Geng Yin and others to hold Yiyang, to block their return route, and charged the generals, "If the bandits flee east, draw the Yiyang troops to join at Xinan;"

sentences.zh: 賊若南走，可引新安兵會宜陽。

translations.literal: if the bandits flee south, you may draw the Xinan troops to join at Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: if they flee south, draw the Xinan troops to join at Yiyang."

sentences.zh: 」馮異與赤眉遇於華陰，相拒六十餘日，戰數十合，降其將卒五千餘人。

translations.literal: " Feng Yi encountered the Red Eyebrows at Huayin; they faced each other for more than sixty days; fought several tens of engagements; and reduced their generals and soldiers by more than five thousand who surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yi met the Red Eyebrows at Huayin; they faced each other for more than sixty days, fought several dozen engagements, and induced more than five thousand of their officers and men to surrender.
